Breaking blocks underneath a hidden menu works again

entries.title: Whitelisted /stopsound for Free Play runs
entries.summary: Running /stopsound to silence a sound no longer marks your run as cheated — it has no gameplay effect, so it's now treated the same as /playanimation, /help, and /me.

entries.title: Chorus no longer blocks the train in the End band
entries.summary: Chorus plants that occasionally grew into the train's path through the floating End-island stretch are now cleared out ahead of the train, so the ride no longer snags on them. The islands and the chorus growing on them off to the sides are left untouched.
highlights: Chorus fruit no longer obstructs the train in the End-island band

entries.title: Kinetic Hosting banner in the modpacks
entries.summary: The Dungeon Train modpacks now bundle the Kinetic Hosting Integration mod, adding a Kinetic Hosting banner to the multiplayer menu. It's on by default and links straight to our hosting partner.
highlights: Kinetic Hosting Integration bundled in both the CurseForge and Modrinth packs, enabled by default
Multiplayer-menu banner links to the Kinetic Hosting affiliate page out of the box

entries.title: Play in 10 more languages
entries.summary: Dungeon Train is now playable in ten more languages — German, French, Italian, European Portuguese, Dutch, Polish, Russian, Japanese, Korean, and Traditional Chinese. Menus, generated item names, in-world books, the death-screen ledger, and the bundled companion mods are all translated, and each language has its own Death Note trigger word. These are AI translations (marked as such on the title screen, with a faded language-menu badge) — native-speaker corrections are very welcome.
highlights: German, French, Italian, European Portuguese, Dutch, Polish, Russian, Japanese, Korean & Traditional Chinese
Menus, item names, books, and death-screen prose all localized
Per-language Death Note trigger titles (デスノート, Тетрадь смерти, 死亡筆記, …)
AI-translated, faded language-menu badge — native-speaker feedback welcome

entries.title: Ride photos no longer jolt your camera
entries.summary: The train's automatic ride photos are now taken completely behind the scenes. Previously the camera would briefly snap to a third-person angle the instant a photo was captured; now your view stays perfectly steady while the memory is saved to your gallery.
highlights: No more camera flicker when a ride photo is taken
Photos are captured invisibly — your view never changes

entries.title: Sharper death-screen photos
entries.summary: Your death-screen ride photo now captures at a much higher resolution, so the scene looks noticeably crisper.
highlights: Ride photos capture at up to 1080p instead of the old lower-res cap
Photos are compressed smartly before sending, keeping load times snappy

entries.title: Tighter, consistent gaps between train carriage groups
entries.summary: The seams between carriage groups on the train now settle at a small, even gap instead of varying in size or occasionally clipping into each other. Also fixes the seam jitter that happened when groups landed too close together.
highlights: Even, small gaps between carriage groups
No more touching/clipping seams or seam jitter

entries.title: New creeper encounter and potion barrel loot
entries.summary: Added a new creeper enemy variant and potion barrel loot to spice up dungeon carriages, along with refreshed barrel layout variants.
highlights: New creeper enemy variant
New potion barrel loot prefab
Updated barrel container variants

entries.title: Loose carriage blocks stay part of the train
entries.summary: Mining part of a carriage no longer breaks a disconnected chunk off into its own drifting mini-ship. Any blocks left floating inside a carriage group now stay welded to the train and ride along with it.
highlights: Disconnected blocks stay attached to the carriage group instead of spawning a separate physics object

entries.title: Loot chests in tunnels now spawn with loot
entries.summary: Loot-linked chests (and other containers) placed inside tunnels were always empty — they now roll their loot when the tunnel generates, just like chests in the train carriages. Each chest rolls its own contents.
highlights: Tunnel loot chests now contain items instead of being empty
Works for both freshly-generated and editor-placed tunnels

entries.title: New loot containers and variants
entries.summary: Added new loot content: creeperdrop, bamboo, crystal, endtower, tnt, enderbooks, and craftcraft variants, plus an updated default tunnel section.

entries.title: Clear stray blocks from the train's path
entries.summary: Fixed rare cases where trees (especially large/dark oak) could leave wood blocking the tracks in the train's path. The corridor now clears anything that strays into the train's collision path, not just leaves.

entries.title: The train smashes through blocks in its path
entries.summary: Build across the tracks and the train no longer glides through your wall like a ghost — it breaks it, with the sound, the particles and the dropped items you would expect. Blocks that appear after the corridor was carved (a wall you built, a tree that grew, a structure the tunnelling missed) used to be passed through invisibly.
highlights: Blocks in the train's path break on contact and drop their items; chests spill their contents.
Only real collisions count — a block drifting through the open deck of a flatbed is left alone, and flowers and grass are brushed past.
The track under the train is never damaged.
Server owners can turn it off per world with /dungeontrain breakblocks off, or globally in the config.

entries.title: Player Mobs move around the train better
entries.summary: Two fixes to how Player Mobs get around. Crossing between carriages, they now take a hop sized to the actual gap — the seams between carriages were tightened a while back, but Player Mobs kept using the big leap they needed for the old wider gaps, so they'd sail across a hand's-width seam. And a Player Mob that falls onto the tracks now works its way back aboard instead of being stranded: it bridges off the rails, builds a pillar up beside the passing carriages, and waits for a clear opening before jumping in.
highlights: Cross-carriage hops are sized to the real gap instead of always being a full sprint leap
Player Mobs that fall onto the track bed climb back aboard instead of getting stuck
Boarding waits for a real opening, so mobs stop leaping into carriage walls

entries.title: Adventure Item Names, Adventure Item Stats, Interactive Player Mobs and Ender Chest Persistence are now separate downloads
entries.summary: These four mods used to be bundled invisibly inside Dungeon Train. They are now normal required dependencies you install alongside it, so each one gets credit on its own mod page. If you use the CurseForge or Modrinth app, or the Dungeon Train modpack, they are fetched automatically and nothing changes for you. If you install the jar by hand, you will be prompted for the four missing mods on first launch and will need to download them too. Discord Presence is still bundled.
highlights: Four bundled mods are now separate required downloads — installed automatically by the CurseForge/Modrinth apps and the modpack
Manual jar installers will be prompted to add the four mods on first launch
Dungeon Train's own jar is about 1.3 MB smaller

entries.title: Armor bar shows your full protection
entries.summary: The modpacks now bundle Overloaded Armor Bar, on by default. Once your armor climbs past a full bar, the extra protection is drawn as stacked coloured icons instead of quietly running out of room to display.
highlights: Overloaded Armor Bar ships enabled by default in the CurseForge and Modrinth modpacks

entries.title: Armor keeps improving past 1.5 bars
entries.summary: Minecraft quietly caps a player's armor at 30 points — one and a half full armor bars — and throws away anything above it. Deep-run gear could promise more armor in its tooltip than the game would ever grant, so late-run armor stopped improving while weapons kept scaling. That ceiling is now raised, and armor toughness along with it.
highlights: Armor above 30 points now actually protects you instead of being silently discarded
Pairs with the Overloaded Armor Bar display so the extra protection is visible too

entries.title: Tunnel chest loot no longer over-powered
entries.summary: Chests found in tunnels were rolling item stats far higher than they should — gear pulled from a tunnel near the start of a run could carry bonuses meant for the deepest part of the line. Tunnel loot now scales from the train's position the same way carriage loot always has.
highlights: Tunnel chests near the start of a run now roll ordinary stats instead of end-game ones
Tunnel and carriage loot at the same point on the line are now on the same power scale
Tunnels already generated in an existing world keep their old loot — only newly generated tunnels are affected

entries.title: Armor above 30 now requires Adventure Item Stats 0.7.0
entries.summary: Minecraft caps armor at 30 points, and past difficulty tier ~25 that ceiling was silently swallowing the armor your gear said it was giving you. Adventure Item Stats 0.7.0 lifts the cap; Dungeon Train now requires that version rather than accepting older builds, so the clamp cannot come back on a stale install. If you are still on 0.6.0 the game will tell you to update on launch.
highlights: Dungeon Train now requires Adventure Item Stats 0.7.0 or newer
Fixes armor silently capping at 30 past difficulty tier ~25

entries.title: Pausing or minimising the game now lets your computer rest
entries.summary: Pausing Minecraft never actually stopped it drawing — it kept rendering the world as fast as your graphics card could manage, so fans stayed loud and laptops kept draining even while you were away from the keyboard. Dungeon Train now caps the frame rate while the game is paused, unfocused, or minimised, and restores it the instant you come back.
highlights: Measured ~105 fps down to 30 while paused, with no delay on un-pause.
Only ever lowers your frame rate — if your Max Framerate is already below the cap, your setting wins.
Adjust or disable with /framerate-throttle, or in the client config.
Automatically off in VR, where a capped frame rate causes motion sickness.

entries.title: Ghasts grow bolder each time you return to the Nether
entries.summary: The Nether band's ghasts have been retuned. Your first trip through is calmer than before — ghasts are an occasional threat instead of a constant swarm, leaving room for the piglins, skeletons and magma cubes that share the band. But every full lap back around to the Nether makes them denser, and lets more of them hover over you at once.
highlights: First Nether: noticeably fewer ghasts than before
Each lap back to the Nether raises how often ghasts appear and how many can crowd you
Ghasts can no longer fill the band on their own — ground mobs keep their share

entries.title: Editor hotkeys stay silent in survival
entries.summary: Pressing the editor menu keys (block-variant, container-contents, template-blocks) while in survival no longer flashes editor status messages on your action bar.
highlights: No more spurious 'requires OP' / 'Not in an editor plot' flashes in survival

entries.title: Suspicious sand on the train digs up real loot
entries.summary: Brushing suspicious sand or gravel found on the train now uncovers a random archaeology find — pottery sherds, gems, and more — just like suspicious sand out in the world. Before, train-placed suspicious blocks brushed up empty.
highlights: Suspicious sand/gravel on carriages now yields archaeology loot when brushed
Same loot resolves every time for a given block (deterministic per carriage)

entries.title: Player-written loot books are now chosen for you
entries.summary: Community books found in chests are now picked per player instead of at random. You'll be handed books you haven't read yet, and the same one won't turn up twice in a life — unless it's still unread and you've left it two whole carriage groups behind. And once you've read a community book, it stays read in every new world you start.
highlights: Prefers books you haven't read yet
Books you've read stay read across brand-new worlds, not just the one you read them in
No repeats within a life, until you've travelled two full carriage groups past where you found one
A slot meant for a player's book now reliably serves one, instead of sometimes falling back to a built-in book
On multiplayer worlds each player gets their own selection, matched to their own language

entries.title: Carriages stay on-theme in the upside-down & end-islands stretches
entries.summary: Fixed the train pulling carriages, rooms and loot from every biome stage at once while crossing the upside-down and end-islands stretches (and around one high-difficulty gap). Those stretches now stay themed to the stage you've actually reached — quartz stays quartz — instead of turning into a jumble of all stages.
highlights: Upside-down and end-islands stretches keep the current stage's theme
No more all-stages jumble around Diff-Level 67-69

entries.title: Truer distance stats behind the scenes
entries.summary: Death and run reports now record how far down the line you actually reached — measured from where you spawned — plus which world band you died in. This sharpens the private stats dashboard only; there is no in-game change.

entries.title: New 'Ways to Help' menu
entries.summary: The title screen now has a Support the Mod button (where Minecraft Realms used to be) plus a Patreon shortcut. It opens a page gathering every way you can help build out Dungeon Train: donate directly, back it on Patreon, use the server-hosting affiliate link when you rent a server, share the mod with content creators, and give feedback or join the Discord.
highlights: Support the Mod + Patreon buttons on the title screen (replacing the Realms button)
Direct donation, Patreon, and a server-hosting affiliate link in one place
Prompts to share the mod with creators and to give feedback / join the Discord

entries.title: Chuncks — a mostly-void band of scattered floating chunks
entries.summary: The train now crosses a new Chuncks region: mostly open void, sprinkled with the occasional real overworld chunk. Some are full-height islands; others are just a floating slab of the surface with a flat cut-off bottom. The void thickens gradually as you approach, and the train keeps rolling across on its floating track. It sits late in the world-gen cycle, after the upside-down band.
highlights: New Chuncks band — mostly void with occasional floating overworld chunks (full-height or top-down slices)
Void ramps in gradually on approach, with an overworld buffer before the band
Fully configurable: band length, void density, slice ratio, entry fade, and lead-in gap

entries.title: New well loot content, plus leatherworker & prefab loot tuning
entries.summary: A new well content piece can now appear aboard the train, and the leatherworker's stock and several loot prefabs (enchant barrel, horse, iron/gold, villager) have been rebalanced.
highlights: New well content set
Leatherworker loot/variant tuning
Rebalanced enchant barrel, horse, iron/gold, and villager loot prefabs

entries.title: Reboard now defaults to Survival
entries.summary: Reboarding from the death screen now always drops you into Survival mode, so a Creative or Spectator run (like Free Play) doesn't silently carry over. Hold Shift while clicking Reboard or Board Anew to keep your current game mode instead — the button turns blue to remind you.
highlights: Reboard forces Survival by default
Hold Shift to preserve your current game mode (button turns blue)

entries.title: In-game update notifications
entries.summary: Dungeon Train now tells you inside the game when a newer version is available — an "Update available" badge appears next to the mod on the Mods screen. It only notifies; it never downloads or changes anything on its own, so you stay in control and update through your launcher as usual.
highlights: "Update available" badge on the Mods screen when you're behind the latest release
Notification only — no auto-download; update via CurseForge / Modrinth / your launcher

entries.title: Official links now stay up to date
entries.summary: The Discord invite, Patreon, donation and hosting-affiliate links now update themselves from the Dungeon Train server whenever you're online, so buttons in the menus always point at the current official destinations — even on older versions of the mod. Offline, the built-in links still work as before.
highlights: Links refresh once per session from the title screen; no account data is sent
Default donation amount is now $25 AUD (was $45)

entries.title: Vote on the books other players wrote
entries.summary: Community books now end with a page from the train itself: it asks whether you enjoyed the book, with thumbs up / thumbs down (or just press Y / N from any page). Voting closes the book, the train answers in chat, and the burn takes your side — green flames for a yes, red for a no, with the usual orange still flickering through. Votes travel back to the rails and quietly shape how often that book is found by other travellers.
highlights: A dimmed, train-voiced vote page appears after the last page of player-written books
Y / N hotkeys vote instantly from any page
Green / red tinted burns for voted books — Death Notes keep their soul burn
Popular books surface more often in loot, panned ones ride quieter

entries.title: Found books always burn again
entries.summary: Fixed a wedge where chest books could get stuck as their built-in stand-in when the community pool had nothing new to offer — they now resolve properly (repeats allowed) and always burn after reading, like any other book of the train.

entries.title: AI label on machine-translated languages
entries.summary: The language-selection list now marks Dungeon Train translations that have not been human-reviewed with a small faded blue AI label next to the Dungeon Train logo, so you can tell at a glance which translations are machine-generated.
highlights: Human-reviewed languages keep the solid logo with no label

entries.title: Same seed, same world: band layout is now seed-deterministic
entries.summary: Creating a world with a fixed seed now always produces the same nether-band mountains, biome front, and band layout — previously each fresh world rolled its own internal layout seed even with the seed box filled in. The band terrain system also now activates before the very first spawn chunks generate, so early chunks can no longer miss band biomes, and any biome-override error is now logged instead of silently baking the wrong biome. Existing worlds are unaffected.
highlights: Fixed-seed worlds now reproduce the same band terrain and biome front
Band biomes can no longer be missing from the first-generated spawn chunks
Silent biome-fallback errors are now logged

entries.title: Faster world generation between special zones
entries.summary: The train's world generator now skips its special-zone terrain work (nether mountains, biome forcing, track-bed checks) on chunks that are provably outside those zones — most of the ride. Chunk streaming in the overworld stretches costs roughly a third less server time, so long rides stay smoother, with terrain byte-identical to before.
highlights: Overworld gaps between zones generate ~25-40% faster; upside-down band ~38% faster
Terrain and biomes are unchanged everywhere — existing worlds continue seamlessly

entries.title: Smoother ticks in the upside-down region
entries.summary: Removed a hidden per-tick cost in the upside-down region: the server was repeatedly re-checking mirrored-terrain chunks that couldn't be processed yet. Those chunks now wait quietly until they're actually ready, cutting that background overhead roughly five-fold.

entries.title: Book voting in your language
entries.summary: The train's vote page now speaks all 19 supported languages — its questions, the (Y)es/(N)o labels, and every chat reply it gives after you vote. Until now the vote page always appeared in English, whatever language you play in.

entries.title: Same seed, same world — for real this time
entries.summary: A follow-up to the seed fix: the last places the mod itself made same-seed worlds differ are now deterministic. Trackside stairs land in the same spots with the same left/right rhythm every time, corridor cleanup always finishes before your world saves, and dungeon chest loot rolls identically for identical seeds.
highlights: Trackside stairs and underground stair shafts now place deterministically (roughly every 100 blocks, alternating sides)
Corridor cleanup finishes at shutdown, so saved worlds are always fully swept
Chest loot in track and tunnel structures is now seed-reproducible

entries.title: Chinese Support-page copy, revised by a community translator
entries.summary: The 'Support the Mod' page's Simplified and Traditional Chinese text has been rewritten by a community translator for a much more natural read. The page also now words itself correctly for your install: modpack players see modpack wording, mod-only players see mod wording.
highlights: All 15 Support-page strings revised in both 简体中文 and 繁體中文
Copy adapts automatically between mod and modpack installs

entries.title: Old worlds clean themselves up when you reboard
entries.summary: Dungeon Train has always been one world per ride — now your save folder agrees. Reboarding after death discards the old world instead of saving it: the run's world is deleted and a fresh one takes its place, so your world list and disk stay clean. A little trash icon next to the reboard button lets you turn this off if you'd rather keep your fallen worlds, and renamed or hand-made worlds are never touched. As the old world slips away, the train sees you off with a rotating farewell line — Chinese players get a few classical sayings of their own.
highlights: Reboarding deletes the old run's world (on by default) — toggle it with the trash icon on the death screen
Only auto-generated run worlds are cleaned up; renamed, hand-made and editor worlds are always kept
New 'Leaving the world behind…' farewell lines during the switch, with classical sayings for Chinese players

entries.title: Per-line translation credits, behind the scenes
entries.summary: Every translated line in all 19 languages now records who produced it — which AI model, or which community translator — and who has human-reviewed it. This is repo-side bookkeeping (nothing changes in-game): it makes unreviewed machine translation easy to find for review passes, and properly credits 老本願's Chinese translation work and 阿世xAsh's Support-page revisions line by line.

entries.title: AI-translation ring in the language list
entries.summary: Each Dungeon Train-translated language in the language menu now wears a blue ring around the DT logo: the filled part of the circle shows how much of that translation is AI-generated without human review. A full ring is pure machine translation; it empties as human translators review lines — Simplified Chinese, the most human-reviewed locale, shows only a thin sliver.
highlights: Blue arc = AI-unreviewed share, drawn clockwise from 12 o'clock over a faint full-circle track
Same 35% blue as the existing AI label; human-reviewed locales keep their solid logo

entries.title: Support-funnel usage telemetry + Finances dashboard
entries.summary: The title screen's Support the Mod, Discord and Patreon buttons — and every link on the Support page — now report anonymous usage counts (clicks, whether the external link was actually opened, and time spent on the page) when network features are consented to. Nothing new is shown in game; the data feeds a new Revenue section on the dt-data explorer's Finances page.
highlights: Consent-gated: no network consent, no telemetry
Tracks clicks, confirm-screen follow-through and time on the Support page
Data explorer Costs page relabelled Finances with a Revenue funnel

entries.title: Changed Adventure Item Stats settings now switch the world to Free Play
entries.summary: Dungeon Train's balance is tuned against Adventure Item Stats' standard settings. If those settings have been changed, the world now runs in Free Play for the session — advancements and stats don't count toward your profile while the change is in place, and everything returns to normal once the standard settings are back. On joining you're told exactly which settings differ, and one click on the chat notice restores the defaults for you, backing up your old settings file first.
highlights: Worlds with modified Adventure Item Stats settings run in Free Play (session-only — restoring the settings restores normal play)
The join notice lists exactly which settings were changed
One-click /fixaisconfig restores the standard settings, backing up your old file first

entries.title: New advancement: Cover me in ...leather?
entries.summary: Wear a full set of leather armor whose rolled stats beat a full vanilla diamond set. Deep-train leather can out-roll diamond — this challenge advancement rewards finding out.
highlights: New challenge advancement in the Dungeon Train tab, under Dungeon Train Explorer
Earnable once loot rolls scale up — realistically around the first Nether band

entries.title: Fixed multi-second freezes caused by dropped items near the train
entries.summary: Items and mobs colliding with parts of the train whose terrain hadn't generated yet could lock the whole game up for many seconds (frozen trading, unresponsive menus, hanging quit). Collision checks no longer force that terrain to generate on the spot.
highlights: No more total freezes when items pile up on or fall off a moving train
Rare cosmetic side effect: an item dropped onto a not-yet-generated part of the train may fall through instead of landing

entries.title: Villagers trade anything — new required mod: Trade Everything
entries.summary: Every villager now has a Trade Anything slot at the top of its trade list. Put any item in and the villager exchanges it for goods it buys, priced by real material worth — crafting and smithing recipes, durability, and enchantments all count. Valuable items pay out emeralds or emerald blocks, and emerald blocks break into emeralds automatically when you buy things, with change returned. Powered by a new companion mod, Trade Everything, bundled inside Dungeon Train.
highlights: Sell junk or treasure to any villager — prices follow material value (16 common items ≈ 1 emerald)
Enchantments and durability change what your gear is worth
Emerald blocks work as big currency: broken only when needed, change given in emeralds
Fully configurable in config/tradeeverything.json

entries.title: Villager trades scale with the train — beyond Master
entries.summary: Train villagers now key entirely off their own carriage: deeper carriages host higher-level traders (Novice near spawn, Master from ~carriage 520), and from carriage 30 the gear they sell keeps growing past vanilla — better enchants every ~100 carriages, stats slightly ahead of the local difficulty, and prices that scale with the enchants (big-ticket items charge emerald blocks). Villagers also buy their own stock back at 10% under their sell price. NOTE: the exchange rates and scaling curves are first-pass and still under balancing review — expect tuning in upcoming releases, and please report trades that feel off.
highlights: Deeper carriages = better traders: levels, enchants, stats and prices all follow the carriage
Enchants keep improving past vanilla Master (every ~100 carriages from carriage 30)
Sell items back to their seller at a 10% margin
Balancing is under active review — feedback welcome

entries.title: Archive tagged death-screen photos to the operator dashboard
entries.summary: Behind the scenes: the ride photos already shown on the death screen are now saved to the developers' data dashboard, each tagged with its moment (scenic/combat/gear/lore/social), biome, world band, difficulty, and cart. Operator tooling only — no in-game change.

entries.title: New Credits page in the main menu
entries.summary: A book icon in the top-right of the title screen opens a Credits page — the people who made Dungeon Train, and everyone who translated it, shown in your language.
highlights: Meet the team: Brennan Hatton (Designer & Developer) and Wilson Taylor (Narrative Director), with photos and bios
Translation credits list every human translator, the languages they worked on, and how much of each they contributed
The whole page, bios included, is translated into all 19 supported languages
A 'Support the Developer' button links to the Ways-to-Help page

entries.title: Sharper ride photos with shaders or Distant Horizons
entries.summary: When you play with Distant Horizons plus a shader pack (or Fabulous graphics), Dungeon Train now captures your death-screen ride photos at a higher resolution — up to 1440p or 2160p depending on your frame rate — instead of the standard 1080p, so those far-horizon, shader-lit vistas keep their detail. Without that combination nothing changes: photos stay at the usual resolution. Each photo also records which graphics setup it was taken with.
highlights: Ride photos captured at up to 1440p/2160p when using Distant Horizons + shaders or Fabulous graphics
Resolution adapts to your frame rate so a busy machine isn't pushed harder
No change for standard setups — photos stay at their usual quality

entries.title: Modpack now includes Sodium + Iris
entries.summary: The Dungeon Train modpack now bundles Sodium for a rendering-performance boost and Iris so you can drop in your own shaderpacks. Both are enabled by default; Iris ships with no shaderpack selected, so there's no performance cost until you add one. (Modpack only — the standalone mod jar is unchanged.)
highlights: Sodium 0.8.12 enabled by default for better FPS
Iris shader loader included — add any shaderpack in the shaderpacks folder to turn on shaders
Perf-neutral out of the box: no shader cost until you enable a pack

entries.title: Dungeon Train settings in the Options menu
entries.summary: Dungeon Train's client settings are now reachable straight from Minecraft's Options screen (both the main menu and the pause menu) via a new 'Dungeon Train…' button under the FOV slider — no need to know the X-menu keybind. The screen gathers the display-scale controls (on their own Editor Settings page), an Internet Connection on/off switch, the ride-photo chat log, and a new Snapshot Max Resolution setting that caps how large your ride photos are captured (AUTO keeps the automatic 1080p–2160p behaviour). Every option has a hover description.
highlights: New 'Dungeon Train…' button in the Options screen (main menu + pause menu)
Snapshot Max Resolution setting caps ride-photo capture size (AUTO = automatic)
Internet Connection toggle to turn all online features on or off
Hover descriptions on every setting

entries.title: Saved ride photos are tagged for the gallery
entries.summary: When you press Save on a ride photo from the death screen, that photo is now flagged as one you chose to keep, so it stands out in the online photo gallery. Only applies when online features are enabled.
highlights: Death-screen 'Save' now marks that photo as user-saved online
A new Saved filter surfaces the photos players kept

entries.title: End Crystals stay with the train
entries.summary: End Crystals placed inside a train carriage used to be left behind the moment the train started moving. They now ride along, locked smoothly to their carriage as it travels — including through curves and Nether transitions.
highlights: End Crystals baked into carriages ride with the train instead of being left at the spawn point
Smooth, jitter-free: the crystal is drawn from the carriage's own motion, so it stays glued to the deck

entries.title: Known cheat mods now switch the world to Free Play
entries.summary: Dungeon Train's balance and global stats assume a level playing field. Installing a known cheat mod (x-ray, automation/cheat clients, and similar) now runs the world in Free Play for the session — advancements and stats don't count toward your profile while the mod is present, the same way changed Adventure Item Stats settings already do. Removing the mod and restarting restores normal play. The known-mod list also updates online, so newly-flagged mods are recognised without a mod update.
highlights: Worlds with a known cheat mod installed run in Free Play (session-only — remove the mod to restore normal play)
The join notice names exactly which cheat mod was detected
Editor and dev commands (editor, save, reset, package, export, import) now switch a normal run to Free Play too

entries.title: Loot enchant levels now scale with how far you've travelled
entries.summary: Naturally-spawned enchanted gear — chest loot, mob equipment and villager trades — is now capped at an enchant level that rises with the carriage difficulty: vanilla levels early on, climbing by one every ten difficulty tiers. This keeps enchant power in line with your progress even when an enchantment cap-remover mod is installed. Without such a mod nothing changes, since loot never rolls above vanilla levels anyway.
highlights: Early-game loot stays at vanilla enchant levels; the ceiling rises the deeper you travel
Applies to chest loot, mob gear and villager trades alike
With an enchant cap-remover mod installed, loot no longer jumps to absurd levels early — it tracks your depth

entries.title: Support the creator from the death screen
entries.summary: A new death-screen page, 'the engine room', shows who funds the game and lets you give via a one-off donation or Patreon.

entries.title: Fixed a rare spawn hang when starting a new world
entries.summary: New worlds could occasionally freeze at the loading screen and drop you into the void instead of onto the train, when water or lava sat near the spawn. The spawn now generates safely and always places you on the train.
highlights: No more falling forever at spawn on a fresh world
Spawns next to water or lava no longer hang the game

entries.title: Your own community books tell you their vote tally
entries.summary: When you come across one of your own player-written books out in the world and pick it up, the train's quiet 'a familiar book…' note can now tell you how it's being received — how many readers gave it a thumbs up, and how many thumbed it down. Only you, the author, ever sees those numbers.
highlights: Hold one of your own community books found in loot: the familiar-book line may now report its 👍/👎 vote tally
Author-only — vote counts are never shown to anyone else holding the same book

entries.title: Trade Everything updated — craftable-item value cap
entries.summary: The bundled Trade Everything mod is updated to 0.2.8. Villager 'Trade Anything' payouts for craftable items are now capped at their component worth, so you can't cheese emeralds by crafting cheap high-value items — enchanted and custom-stat gear stay exempt. Also includes refreshed default trade values.
highlights: Craftable items pay out no more than their raw material worth
Enchanted / custom-stat items remain exempt from the cap

entries.title: Modpack: Jade block tooltips now work on the moving train
entries.summary: The Dungeon Train modpack now enables Jade (the block/item tooltip HUD) by default and bundles Jade Sable Compat, a small client-only mod that fixes Jade's tooltips on the moving train. Jade used to ship off because its tooltips read the wrong block when you looked at anything riding a Sable carriage; with the compat mod they now resolve the correct block on the train deck, so Jade is on out of the box. (Modpack only — the standalone mod jar is unchanged.)
highlights: Jade enabled by default in the modpack
Block/item tooltips now read correctly for blocks on the moving train
Bundled Jade Sable Compat (client-only; auto-skipped on dedicated servers)

entries.title: Creepers no longer leave a potion cloud when they explode
entries.summary: Train creepers were picking up the difficulty system's potion buffs, and vanilla turns a creeper's active effects into a lingering potion cloud when it blows up. Creepers now explode cleanly again.

entries.title: Simplified Chinese revision pass
entries.summary: Community translator 老本願 has revised the Simplified Chinese translation, reworking 84 lines across the credits, support, book-voting and death screens for a more natural voice. Every line of Simplified Chinese is now human-translated or human-reviewed — the faded AI marker beside 简体中文 in the language list is gone.
highlights: 84 machine-translated lines rewritten by hand, and the rest checked over
No unreviewed machine translation left in Simplified Chinese

entries.title: WeChat Pay for players in China
entries.summary: Chinese players had no working way to chip in: Patreon is blocked in mainland China, and the direct-donation link needs an overseas card. If your game is set to Chinese, the Ways to Help page and the death-screen Contribute window now offer WeChat Pay instead of Patreon, and the payment page opens in your own language.
highlights: WeChat Pay on the Ways to Help page and the death-screen Contribute window, for clients set to Chinese
The payment page opens in your language instead of guessing from your browser
Your name travels with the donation, so contributions can show on the in-game supporter list
The Patreon shortcut is hidden on those clients rather than leading somewhere unreachable

entries.title: Free Play echoes stay in Free Play
entries.summary: Deaths on a Free Play (creative/cheated) run are now sealed off from normal play. An echo of someone who died in Free Play — and a Death Note curse written in Free Play — will only ever appear to other players who are themselves in Free Play; a legit run only meets echoes and curses from other legit runs. No more sandbox deaths leaking into real games, or vice versa.
highlights: Reincarnated echoes are tagged with the run they came from and only spawn in a matching run.
Death Note curses match the same way: a curse authored in Free Play only hunts Free Play targets.

entries.title: Backers' names ride the train
entries.summary: People who back the project can have their name woven into the train's own language. Their name turns up on weapons you loot, on travellers you meet, and in what the people aboard say to you — mixed in among the community names already there. Nothing is bought that changes how the game plays; it is a name in a hat, drawn at random like all the others.
highlights: Backer names appear on generated gear, mobs, PlayerMobs and in NPC dialogue
Backers can also write a short phrase, which shows up in item lore and traveller dialogue
Every name and phrase is screened before it can appear in anyone's world

entries.title: End cities on the End band's islands
entries.summary: The End band's floating islands are no longer empty. End cities generate on them exactly as they do in the real End — the same spacing, the same end_highlands and end_midlands restriction, the same purpur towers, bridges and end ships, with their loot chests, shulkers and elytra intact. Cities always stand on solid island, and one that lands on the track lane gets punched straight through by the train.
highlights: End cities generate on the End band's islands, at real-End density
End ships, shulkers, end-city loot and elytra come with them
New disintegrationEndCities config key turns them off

entries.title: Shared carriages — community-built rooms that travel between trains
entries.summary: Some carriages can now be shared spaces. Build in one and your room travels to the Dungeon Train relay, where it can later turn up in another player's train — and theirs in yours, arriving exactly as its author left it, loot and all. A build only ever reappears in the same stage of the run it was made in, so a stone-era room won't surface in the deep dark. This is off by default: a server has to switch it on, and uploading anything also needs your network consent.
highlights: Build in a shared carriage and the room travels to other players' trains
Community rooms only appear in the stage of the run they were created in
Stepping into one tells you whether it is untouched or someone has already shaped it
Report a room you would rather not have seen with /reportcarriage
Off by default — a server must enable sharedCarriagesEnabled, and uploads need network consent

entries.title: Your own shared carriages find their way back to you
entries.summary: Shared carriages you build no longer disappear into the pool for good. Around a third of shared carriage slots now hand you back a room you built yourself — travelled out to other players' worlds and returned, exactly as you last left it — while most slots still show you someone else's work and a few stay blank canvases. A carriage you've already met won't turn up twice in the same world, and builds only ever reappear in the kind of place they were made. Creative and survival keep entirely separate pools, so a room built in Free Play never turns up in a survival run, or the other way round.
highlights: About 30% of shared carriage slots return a build of your own, 65% show another player's, and 5% stay a fresh blank canvas
Stepping into one of your own builds says so
No shared carriage repeats within the same world
Free Play and normal play have separate carriage pools that never mix

entries.title: Developer replies stay in your chat history
entries.summary: A reply from the developer used to vanish from the title-screen chat panel: the panel treated it as an automated report and hid it, so a message you had read once was gone the next time you looked. It now stays in your conversation where you can find it again.
highlights: Developer replies remain in the title-screen chat backscroll instead of disappearing on the next launch

entries.title: Shared carriages now credit the people who built them
entries.summary: Step into a carriage that has travelled from another world and it tells you whose hands shaped it — the original builder, and the travellers who changed it along the way.
highlights: A shared carriage names its original builder plus its five most recent contributors when you step aboard.
On a build of your own that has come back around, it skips your name and tells you who has changed it while it was away.
Your name only travels with your work if you have granted network consent; without it your builds are shared exactly as before, just uncredited.
Fixed the carriage entry message printing twice when you jumped inside a carriage.

entries.title: New crafting carriage content variants
entries.summary: The crafting carriage's loot pool now includes two new variant setups, craft2 and enchant2, discovered via the in-game content editor.
highlights: New craft2 content variant
New enchant2 content variant

entries.title: Play-mode telemetry for the data explorer
entries.summary: The world-info report the game already sends on join now notes whether that session was multiplayer, so the private data dashboard can show how the player base splits between single-player, multiplayer, and both. No change to how the game plays.

entries.title: Trade Everything: damaged items no longer overpriced
entries.summary: Updated the bundled Trade Everything sibling mod so damaged items no longer sell for more than pristine ones in a villager's Trade Anything slot.
highlights: Fixed damaged items overpricing in Trade Anything trades

entries.title: Adult and Kid modes
entries.summary: The first-launch screen now asks who is playing. Kid mode turns off chat with the developer and limits player-written books to those an AI has checked as suitable for children — screening for sexual, frightening or cruel content, personal details, and anyone trying to strike up a private conversation. Carriages built by other players are filtered the same way, though a build with no writing in it has nothing to check. You can still write and share your own books and carriages either way. Adult mode is everything, exactly as before, and the setting can be changed anytime in Options.
highlights: Choose Adult or Kid on the first-launch screen, or in Options → Dungeon Train…
Kid mode: no developer chat, and only kid-safe player-written books and carriages
Hover any line on the screen to see exactly what it does
Adult mode is unchanged — existing worlds keep every feature they had

entries.title: Political Content Filter for Chinese-language players
entries.summary: Players on a Chinese-language client are asked once whether to filter out community books and player-written letters that touch on politically sensitive topics. Say yes and they are quietly left out of what you are shown; say no and nothing changes. You can change your answer any time in Options > Dungeon Train.
highlights: Asked once on the title screen, and changeable later from Options > Dungeon Train.
Applies to community books found in chests and to player-written narrative letters.
Your answer is yours alone — on a shared world other players are unaffected by it.

entries.title: The settings screen and the first-launch card now speak all 19 languages
entries.summary: Dungeon Train's own settings screen (Options → Dungeon Train…) and the first-launch 'connect to the internet?' card used to be English no matter what language you play in — so the Adult/Kid question, the five things the card asks about, and the settings you'd go back to in order to change them were unreadable unless you read English. Both are now fully translated, along with the ride-photo options, the familiar-book vote counts, the messages you get when boarding a shared carriage, /report_carriage replies, and the Alipay/WeChat support options. These are machine translations (Claude Opus 5), not yet checked by a human translator — the AI ring in the language list shows how much of your language that covers.
highlights: Options → Dungeon Train… is translated end to end: every row and every hover description
The first-launch internet card — the Adult/Kid choice, all five bullet points and their hover text, and the confirm button
Also translated: ride-photo settings, familiar-book vote counts, shared-carriage arrival messages, /report_carriage, and the Alipay/WeChat support options
Machine translation credited as such — Simplified Chinese's human-reviewed lines are untouched, and the new lines are flagged for a translator's review

entries.title: The AI badge is showing on Simplified Chinese again
entries.summary: Simplified Chinese was marked as human-reviewed in the language list — no AI badge, solid logo — because a community translator had been through every line. This release adds about 103 machine-translated lines to it (the settings screen and the first-launch card), which no human has checked yet, so the badge and its blue ring are back until a translator works through them. Nothing about the translation itself got worse; the label just tells the truth about the new lines.
highlights: Simplified Chinese shows the faded AI label again, with the ring at roughly 10% — the share of lines that are machine-translated and unreviewed
It goes back to a solid logo once those lines have been reviewed

entries.title: What We Give? What Comes Back?
entries.summary:
#### What can we give to the train?

It has given you much. Carriages, corridors, the dark ahead. What is there to give back?

A room. That is what it asks, and what it takes.

Build one in the right place and it does not stay with you. The train carries it off — onto another line, into a world you will never see. And it brings you what others gave: a space you did not make, left exactly so by someone who was gone before you arrived.

Give enough and it gives back. A room of yours comes round again, still as you left it — mostly. Other hands have been in it since.

Who built this? Who has been here since? The carriage remembers, if you ask it.

#### And to the one who laid the track?

Players in China had no way to answer — WeChat Pay now sits on Ways to Help and the death screen, for clients set to Chinese.

#### Who keeps the kids safe, when no-one else is around?

First launch asks who is playing. Kid mode closes the developer chat and lets through only the player-written books and carriages an AI has judged fit for children. Adult is everything, as before.

#### And what of our Chinese players, who must obey the laws of the land?

Filter out the community books and letters that touch politically sensitive ground.

#### What else?
highlights: Updated translations thanks to 老本願
End cities in the End
Effect-less creepers — no lingering potion cloud
Free Play echoes locked to Free Play
Trades more balanced
Dev replies stay in your chat history

entries.title: Shared carriages are actually switched on
entries.summary: They shipped with their master switch off, so no one ever met one. Now on by default, including on worlds you have already been playing.

entries.title: Drifting carriages: a new name and four advancements
entries.summary: Shared carriages are now called drifting carriages — carriages that come loose down the line and reattach to someone else's train. Four new advancements track what you do with them: shaping one nobody has touched, rearranging one a stranger built, having your own come back around to you, and leaving an item in a chest for whoever rides it next. Items you leave in a carriage chest now actually travel with it — before this, a gift left in a chest was never uploaded.
highlights: Shared carriages renamed to drifting carriages, in every language
New advancements: Leaving Marks, Uninvited Renovations, Full Circle, Something For The Next One
Items left in a drifting carriage's chest now ride along for the next traveller to find
Cover me in ...leather? is hidden until you earn it

entries.title: A Drift Gift
entries.summary: The chest-gift advancement introduced in 0.533.0 as "Something For The Next One" is now called "A Drift Gift". Same advancement, same requirement — leave an item in a chest aboard a drifting carriage; only the name changed.
highlights: "Something For The Next One" renamed to "A Drift Gift", in every language

entries.title: Someone aboard has been keeping notes
entries.summary:
There is a passenger who stopped reading books for what they say, and started reading them for how they arrive — which book reaches whose hands, in what tongue, how often. They kept a ledger. Copies of it have started turning up in the carriages.

Whether the train arranged any of it, or the one who built the train, the ledger declines to say.

entries.title: Three new books ride the train
entries.summary: Three new books turn up in chests. One is a traveller's field notes on drifting carriages — how to tell one from a carriage the train built, and what it means to find a chest somebody filled on purpose. The other two ask for help keeping the line running: one a reverent tract, one a plain-spoken passenger who is slightly embarrassed to be raising it at all.
highlights: New book: The Drifting Carriages — recognising a drifting carriage, and what to do in someone else's room
New book: The Second Offering — a tract on the one offering the Creator never asks you for
New book: The Creator's Burden — a plainer account of what the line costs, and where to find the Support screen
New glossary entries for drifting carriages and drift-gifts, and two new quiet rules

entries.title: Your name is filled in on the China payment page
entries.summary: Players paying with WeChat Pay no longer have to type their Minecraft name at checkout — it arrives already filled in, so the support is credited to the right person on the leaderboard.
highlights: The name field is prefilled and the page appears in your own language
You can buy more than one at a time without going through checkout twice

entries.title: Drifting carriages only record real changes
entries.summary: A drifting carriage used to count every door swing and pressure-plate step as an edit, so a carriage nobody had touched could pile up hundreds of recorded changes. Now only changes to the build itself count — placing, breaking, and leaving things behind. Walking through a carriage leaves it exactly as you found it.
highlights: Doors, pressure plates, buttons and levers no longer register as edits to a drifting carriage
Real building — placing, breaking, gifts left in chests — is recorded as before

entries.title: Drifting carriages turn up more often
entries.summary: Drifting carriages — the ones other players have built and left on the line — were rare enough that a long run could pass without one. They now appear about three times as often.

entries.title: Cursed books — find out what your Death Note did
entries.summary: Sign a Death Note, die, and your echo goes hunting in a world you will never see. Until now that was the end of it for you. Now, once your curse actually lands, the next lightning strike brings you a black-violet book telling the story of it: who it found, the carriage it waited at, how long it waited, what it was still carrying, how the fight went, and how it ended. One story per curse — read it and it is gone; ignore it and it comes back next life.
highlights: A cursed welcome book, delivered when one of your Death Note curses lands
The whole encounter, not just the outcome: gear, the beats of the fight, and who walked away
Three books, one per ending — your echo won, they won, or nobody ever found out
Delivered at your next spawn, or between carts if the curse lands mid-run
Death Note echo encounters now post their story to the Discord feed like any other echo

entries.title: New found book: Where the Writing Goes
entries.summary: A new book to find in the train's chests. Eight passengers, eight separate accounts, all circling the same discovery: they kept writing books that burned, until each of them worked out what a lectern does with a book you write on it.
highlights: Eight complete variants — each spawn gives you one, and you won't be shown the same one twice until you've seen them all.
No mechanics change: this is writing about the lectern letters the mod already has, from the point of view of people finding them out the hard way.

entries.title: Where the Writing Goes, in 19 languages
entries.summary: The found book added last release is now readable in every language the mod supports — all eight accounts, translated.
highlights: Machine-translated (Opus 5) and marked as such in the translation credits, so a human translator can review it later.

entries.title: Resetting the train no longer strands drifting carriages
entries.summary: Spawning a fresh train used to quietly abandon any drifting carriages riding on the old one: edits you'd made to them were lost along with the deleted train, and the builds stayed locked to your world for up to an hour before anyone else could receive them. They're now handed back properly before the old train is taken apart. The reset command itself also got two fixes — it always places the new train on the track now, instead of wherever you happened to be standing, and it can no longer leave you with no train at all.
highlights: Edits you made to a drifting carriage survive a train reset instead of vanishing with the old train.
Drifting carriage builds return to the pool straight away, rather than staying locked to your world until they time out.
The train always spawns on the track, and you're set down on the flatbed once it settles.
Removed the carriage count from the spawn command — passing zero deleted your train and then refused to build a new one. Set the window with '/dungeontrain carriages' instead.

entries.title: Love Notes — an echo that comes back loving you
entries.summary: The Death Note has a mirror. Sign a book titled "Love Note" naming another player and it burns away in pink flame instead of soul-fire. When you later die, an echo of you waits for them at the carriage depth you fell at — and greets them instead of hunting them. It hands over what it is carrying, steps in when something attacks them, and never once raises a hand to them. Same book and quill, same price (you still have to die first), opposite intent.
highlights: The echo arrives with the highest possible regard for the one you named: it greets rather than attacks, gives them what it has, and defends them even when badly outmatched.
Once your Love Note lands, your next lightning strike brings you its story — how they took it, and whether they took it at all.
A new advancement, Loved Back, for giving something back to the echo that came all that way for you.
Every language has its own Love Note title, and naming your book that works too.

entries.title: Recommend your favourite mods from the death screen
entries.summary: If you play with mods beyond Dungeon Train and its modpack, the death screen now has a new page asking which of them you'd recommend to the creator. Your mods appear as a grid, ordered by how many other Dungeon Train players run them. Pick one, say why in a line, and send — then pick another, as many as you like. There's also a tile for naming a mod you don't have but wish the train supported. Nothing is sent unless you write something, and the page only ever appears if you're running mods of your own.
highlights: New death-screen page: recommend the mods you play with
Your mods are ranked by how many other players run them
Ask for a mod you don't have yet
Only appears if you run mods outside Dungeon Train and its modpack

entries.title: Death screen financial numbers updated
entries.summary: The support page's figures have been reworked.

entries.title: Editing a weight no longer unlinks a template from its Stage
entries.summary: In the in-world editor, changing the weight of a carriage, contents, or track-side variant that was linked to a Stage silently detached it — the row quietly stopped following its Stage and froze on whatever stale spawn gate had been snapshotted. Weight and gate edits now keep the Stage link.
highlights: Affects all three weight editors: carriages, carriage contents, and track-side variants.
Templates already unlinked by this bug cannot be recovered automatically — the link is gone from disk and needs setting again in the editor.
Editing a spawn gate by command on a Stage-linked template now warns that the inline gate won't take effect until you detach the template to Custom.

entries.title: Pick an amount: three price points on the support pages
entries.summary: The Ways to Help page and the death-screen Contribute window now lead with three named amounts instead of asking you to invent one — $10 Help The Dev, $30 A Big Fan, and $70 Server Costs, which covers a whole month of running the servers. Each opens a checkout with your player name already filled in. Giving a custom amount or setting up a monthly pledge on Patreon are both still there, tucked underneath.
highlights: Three named amounts on both support screens: $10, $30 and $70 AUD
$70 covers a full month of Dungeon Train's server costs
Custom Amount and Recurring are still available below the three amounts
Translated into all 19 languages

entries.title: Carriages you've walked away from stop running their mobs
entries.summary: A long train used to keep every mob in every carriage you had already passed thinking at full speed, forever. Now, once every player has been more than 55 blocks from a carriage for a few seconds, that carriage's mobs are set aside — and restored the moment someone comes back, exactly as you left them: villager trades, gear, inventories, names and positions all intact. Half-loot a carriage, wander off, come back, and you'll find what you left rather than a fresh roll. This mostly helps dedicated servers and multiplayer, where mobs on carriages nobody is near were pure overhead. You may occasionally spot mobs in a far-off carriage blink out and reappear as you get closer; that's this at work.
highlights: Mobs on carriages no player is near are stored instead of running AI
Restored exactly as you left them — villager trades and half-looted state included
Server operators can toggle it with /dungeontrain debug contentsdespawn on|off|status

entries.title: New "Dungeon Train (Flat)" world type
entries.summary: Creating a world now offers "Dungeon Train (Flat)" alongside the usual Dungeon Train option. The train runs across level ground with no terrain generation at all, which makes it a calm place to build, test contraptions, or just watch the train without the landscape getting in the way. One thing to know before you pick it: because nothing is generated around the track, the shifting terrain bands don't appear either — no disintegration stretch and no Nether transition. Choose the normal Dungeon Train world type if you want those.
highlights: Pick "Dungeon Train (Flat)" from the world type list when creating a world
Level ground the whole way, with no terrain generation
Band content (disintegration, Nether transition) does not generate in flat worlds

entries.title: Simplified Chinese: full human translation review
entries.summary: 老本願 has reviewed Dungeon Train's Simplified Chinese translation end to end. 97 interface lines were rewritten and 18 confirmed, taking 简体中文 to 96.5% human-reviewed — the menus, consent screens, advancements and shared-carriage messages now read as written Chinese rather than machine translation. Four in-world books were translated for the first time, so every random book you can find now has a Chinese edition, and two more picked up their newest entries.
highlights: 97 interface lines rewritten by a human translator, 18 confirmed
Four in-world books translated into Chinese for the first time — full coverage
New drifting-carriage entries added to Quiet Rules and the Train Glossary
简体中文 now shows as human-reviewed in the language list

entries.title: Your mod recommendations reach the creator
entries.summary: When you recommend a mod on the death screen — or ask for one that isn't supported yet — the reason you write is now sent along with it, so Brennan can actually read why. Requests keep the name you typed, which is the only name they have.
highlights: The mod you name and the reason you give travel together, instead of the reason living only in a Discord channel
Asking for a mod that isn't supported now records what you asked for, not just that you asked

entries.title: Discord and Support the Mod are now in the pause menu
entries.summary: The two links that used to live only on the main menu are now a keypress away mid-run. Press Esc and you'll find Discord and Support the Mod where Minecraft's Feedback and Report Bugs buttons used to sit — bug reports for Dungeon Train go through the mod's own report form on the death screen, so those vanilla links were pointing at the wrong place anyway.
highlights: Discord invite reachable from the in-game Esc menu
Support the Mod reachable without quitting to the main menu

entries.title: Mod recommendations now come after the support page
entries.summary: On the death screen, the page asking which of your other mods you'd recommend now appears after the support page, just before you board again. Same pages, new order.
highlights: Mod recommendations moved after 'support the line'

entries.title: Fix your language's own text, from inside the game
entries.summary: Dungeon Train speaks nineteen languages besides English, and most of those lines were written by a machine. If one of them reads wrong to you, you can now fix it yourself: Options → Language → Help Translate opens the mod's whole vocabulary, line by line, with the English original beside each one and your language's current wording ready to edit. Send your fixes in and, once a human has read them, they reach everyone playing in that language — no update to install. Your name goes on them in the credits, unless you would rather it did not.
highlights: Help Translate sits on the language screen, and on the title screen beside the language button
Every line the mod ships, with filters for what a human has never checked
Work in a batch and send it when it is ready — nothing leaves the game until you press Submit
Approved fixes arrive when the game starts or you change language
A fix applies to the version it was written against and later ones, so an old fix never overwrites newer wording
Export and import the files if you would rather work outside the game
Translators are named in the credits, and the language list's AI marker retreats as lines get human-checked
Submitting needs network consent, like everything else that carries your name

entries.title: Each difficulty is now its own run
entries.summary: Peaceful, Easy, Normal and Hard each keep their own gear, XP, Ender Chest and echoes. Switch difficulty and you switch profiles — what you were carrying is waiting for you when you switch back, and nothing you farmed on an easier setting comes with you.
highlights: Your Ender Chest is now per-difficulty, and so is the inventory and XP carried between runs when keepInventory is on.
An Ender Chest that isn't your default one says so in its title — "Ender Chest (Hard)", "(Adventure · Hard)" or "(Free Play)" — so an empty chest never looks like lost items.
Echoes only return on the difficulty they died on, so a Hard run never meets a Peaceful ghost.
Changing difficulty in-game tells you in chat which profile you moved to and where your gear is waiting.
Normal keeps everything you already have — existing Ender Chests and past lives all belong to Normal, so nothing goes missing.

entries.title: The death screen recap now works in multiplayer
entries.summary: Dying on a server used to give you Minecraft's plain death screen. Now you get the same end-of-run recap singleplayer gets — your fall, your deeds, your cargo, your ride photos and the rest — with Respawn in place of the board-a-new-train button, since a server world isn't yours to restart.
highlights: The narrative death screen now appears on LAN and dedicated servers
Respawn replaces Board anew there, and the delete-world toggle is hidden

entries.title: Difficulty set by command no longer follows you into a new world or a new life
entries.summary: Setting the difficulty by command — /dungeontrain difficulty, or the difficulty /dtp applies when it drops you somewhere far down the line — used to be written once and left everywhere: start a brand-new world and it opened at whatever tier you last set, and dying didn't undo it either, so a fresh run carried on at a difficulty it never earned. That setting now belongs to the world you set it in. A new world starts on automatic, dying puts you back on automatic, and the world you set it in still remembers it when you come back.
highlights: A newly created world no longer inherits a difficulty set in another world
Dying resets the difficulty back to automatic — the new run scales from real travel again
Reloading the world you set it in keeps the difficulty you set
On a server with other players still riding, one player's death leaves the difficulty alone

entries.title: Train Dimensions — doors on the train that open somewhere else
entries.summary: Somewhere past your first stretch of track, a corridor between two carriages stops being a corridor. Walk it and the sound of the train falls away behind you, and you come out in a room that could never have fitted inside the carriage you stepped into — a hall, a library, a place of beams and sculk, some of them going on for as long as you care to keep walking. What you find is drawn from how far you have come, so late portals open onto places the early ones never do, and every portal rolls its own room: chests you loot stay looted when you walk back in. The train keeps rolling while you look around, and the ground you cover in there counts toward your journey. Nothing strands you — there is always a way back out — and if you would rather the door weren't there at all, breaking through the corridor's outer wall closes that portal for good.

entries.title: Editor: middle-click copies a cell's block variants
entries.summary: In the block-variant editor, middle-clicking a cell that has variants now puts that cell's whole variant list in your hand as a clipboard item — no opening the Z menu, no hunting through your backpack for it. If the same clipboard is already on your hotbar it just switches to that slot, and middle-clicking anything else still does a normal pick-block.
highlights: Middle-click a variant cell to copy it straight to your hotbar
Switches to the matching clipboard when you already have one
Vanilla pick-block still works on every other block

entries.title: Resizing a portal room now grows it from both ends
entries.summary: In the room editor, the length and width steppers alternate which wall moves, so a room grows outwards from what you have built instead of always off the far end. Shrinking is no longer one-way: the row you crop is remembered for this world, and stepping the size back up puts those blocks, their variants and their chest contents back exactly as they were. Resizing also keeps whatever you have built since your last save, and Reset now puts a room's dimensions back along with its blocks.
highlights: Length and width grow and shrink from alternating ends; height still moves only its ceiling
A row removed by shrinking comes back if you grow the room again
Resizing no longer discards edits made since your last save
Reset restores the saved size, not just the saved blocks

entries.title: Villagers price up the item you are holding
entries.summary: Updated the bundled Trade Everything mod. A villager's Trade Anything slot now cycles through what it will take and previews the price for the item you are currently holding, so you can see what a trade is worth before you make it.
highlights: Held-item price preview in the Trade Anything slot
Cycling Trade Anything icon

entries.title: More variety in one of the small path rooms
entries.summary: A pass over the pathssmall portal room: more of its blocks now vary between copies, and more of its containers roll from curated pools, so repeat visits look and loot differently.

entries.title: Breaking into a portal corridor closes it for good
entries.summary: Dig through the outer wall of a portal corridor past the halfway point and the portal breaks — glass shatters, a beacon dies away, and that portal never takes you through again. You can always still walk back out of a portal room, so a broken portal can strand nothing and nobody.
highlights: Breaking a portal corridor's outer wall past the halfway point permanently closes it
Both ends of a portal close together — one hole shuts the whole thing
The way back out always works, so you can never be trapped in a portal room
Digging inside a portal room, or before the halfway point, is safe

entries.title: Portal transitions no longer flash
entries.summary: Stepping through a portal corridor used to flash the world for a moment on the other side — sometimes a wash of pale sky, sometimes the skybox showing through where the room should be. The arrival is now drawn properly, so walking a portal looks like walking through a doorway.
highlights: No flash on arriving in a portal room, in either direction
Endless portal rooms no longer white out as their fog comes in

entries.title: Portal rooms can hold enemies, and no two corridors are alike
entries.summary: Step through a portal and the corridor you walk isn't always the same one — each portal furnishes its own. The pocket room beyond can be home to something, too: rooms are authored with the creatures that live in them, and an endless room keeps them coming as it unfolds around you.
highlights: Portal rooms can be home to creatures, placed by whoever built the room
Each portal's corridors are furnished from their own set, so no two portals read the same

entries.title: The void around a bedrockless portal room closes in as you walk out
entries.summary: Some portal rooms are built standing in empty space rather than sealed in rock. Walking off one of those and out into the emptiness used to look exactly like standing still in it — the same haze at every distance. The fog now thickens the further out you get, until the room you left has vanished and the dark has no edge you can find.
highlights: Fog closes in progressively as you walk away from a bedrockless portal room
Walk far enough and the room behind you disappears entirely
Fixed: the fog used to cut out the moment you stepped off the structure, instead of thickening

entries.title: Portal rooms no longer fill up with broken blocks and doubled-up mobs
entries.summary: A portal's room was being torn down and rebuilt over and over as the train rolled, instead of being built once. Every rebuild left the room a little more cluttered: pressure plates popped off their supports and their drops stayed floating where they broke, and the room's own mobs were carried over and then spawned again beside themselves. A room is now laid down once, and stays as it was built.
highlights: Fixed: floating dropped items piling up in portal rooms, where blocks had been broken by a rebuild
Fixed: a portal room's mobs appearing twice over, growing every time the train travelled
Portal rooms are built once instead of being repeatedly re-laid as the train moves

entries.title: The music fades out as you walk into a portal
entries.summary: Head down a portal corridor and the soundtrack sinks away with every step, gone by the time you reach the door. Portal rooms are silent — nothing plays in there, however long you stay. Walk back out onto the train and the music doesn't come blaring back mid-song either; the quiet holds for a while, then a fresh track starts on its own.
highlights: Music fades out over the last stretch of a portal corridor
Portal rooms are completely silent
No jarring mid-track resume when you come back to the train

entries.title: Walking through a portal no longer counts as leaving the train
entries.summary: Stepping through a hallway portal used to look, to the game, exactly like jumping off the side of the train — so a walk to a portal room and back handed out Off the Rails and Back on Board for using a door. Those awards, and the one for shoving a passenger off the train, now ignore everything that happens beneath the world's bedrock, which is where portal rooms are built. Leaving the train the honest way still earns them, and shoving an echo into the void still earns Into the Void.
highlights: Portal trips no longer award Off the Rails or Back on Board
Leading a punched passenger through a portal no longer counts as shoving them off the train
Genuinely leaving the train, and voiding an echo, still earn their advancements

entries.title: The endless portal rooms now carry on past their tunnels
entries.summary: In an endless portal room, the tunnels back to the train stand inside the room rather than at its edge — but the ground gave out around them. Walk round the side of one and the floor simply stopped: open void, with the tunnel hanging in it. The room now continues past its tunnels, laying its own floor, ceiling and walls right up to them, so a tunnel reads as something standing in the hall that you can walk around. Open-walled endless rooms carry their floor and ceiling through in the same way.
highlights: Fixed: void where the floor should be, in the aisles either side of a portal room's tunnels
An endless room's own walls and ceiling now continue around its tunnels
The way back to the train is still a wall with a door in it, unchanged

entries.title: Monsters no longer spawn in the empty dark below the world
entries.summary: Portal rooms are built in an empty basement beneath the world's bedrock, and the game still treated that space as somewhere ordinary monsters could turn up — on a room's roof, in the gap just outside its walls, or anywhere else down there the dark reached. Nothing arrives on its own below the bedrock now. The mobs a portal room is built with are unaffected, and so is anything you bring down there yourself.
highlights: Fixed: skeletons and zombies gathering around portal rooms, below the world's bedrock
Nothing spawns of its own accord beneath the bedrock layer
A portal room's own mobs, and any you lead in yourself, are untouched

entries.title: Nothing generates in the empty space beneath the world
entries.summary: The space under the world's bedrock is kept clear for portal rooms, but structures anchored at a fixed depth — trial chambers, ancient cities — were resolving into it and building there anyway: sealed beneath the bedrock, impossible to reach, and pointed at by /locate as though you could go and find them. Nothing generates below the bedrock now, and a structure that straddles it keeps only the part that reaches real ground.
highlights: Fixed: trial chambers and ancient cities generating below the world's bedrock, out of reach
/locate no longer sends you after a structure buried under the bedrock
The space beneath the bedrock stays clear for portal rooms

entries.title: Cave noises carry through the portal rooms
entries.summary: A portal room is meant to feel a long way from the train: the soundtrack fades out as you walk the tunnel and there is none at all once you are inside. That left the rooms completely silent, which read as nothing there rather than somewhere else. The old familiar cave noises now turn up while you are in a portal room — the same distant groans and drips you get deep underground, drifting in from somewhere past the walls every half-minute to a few minutes. They stop at the room: the tunnels back to the train still carry the engine and the last of the music, and nothing follows you back aboard.
highlights: Cave noises now play while you are inside a portal room
They come and go on their own, roughly every 30 seconds to 3 minutes
The tunnels back to the train are unchanged — engine and fading music as before
Controlled by the Ambient volume slider, like cave noises anywhere else

entries.title: Every portal room is its own room
entries.summary: Portal rooms all looked the same. Two portals that drew the same kind of room were identical down to the block — same walls, same chests, same contents — so the tenth portal you walked was the first one again. Each portal now rolls its own room, from where it sits on the train. Walk back into one you've already been through and it is still the room you left, chests and all.
highlights: Each portal's room rolls its own blocks, chests and furnishings
Rooms you have already looted stay looted when you walk back in

entries.title: Portal rooms are themed to how far you have travelled
entries.summary: The room behind a portal is no longer drawn from the whole pool every time. Each room — and each of its sub-variants — can now be limited to a stretch of the run, so early portals open onto different places than late ones. Comes with a batch of authored rooms: a new zombie room, furnished starting rooms with loot chests and mobs, and reworked beam and sculk rooms.
highlights: Portal rooms are drawn to match your progress through the run
New zombie portal room
The starting portal rooms are furnished with loot chests, mobs and more block variety
Reworked beam and sculk rooms

entries.title: Portal rooms stop breaking their own furnishings
entries.summary: Furnishing a portal room knocked loose whatever was resting on the floor it was decorating. The single-pillar room showed it worst: the ring of pressure plates around the pillar was broken off and left lying on the floor as items, every time, alongside a fresh set of plates.
