Rooms are now furnished without disturbing anything standing on them.
highlights: Portal rooms no longer scatter broken pieces of their own furnishings across the floor
Furnishing a room takes half the block updates it used to

entries.title: More ways out of an endless portal room
entries.summary: The rooms behind a portal that repeat forever used to have exactly one way back to the train, however far you wandered. They can now scatter extra corridors through themselves, so there is usually another way out somewhere near you. Walk back in through one and you return to where you left, rather than to the start. Some rooms hide the way onward as well: the door directly opposite the one you arrived by may be nothing but more room, and the real one is somewhere else in the maze. Corridor doorways are also built from the room's own walls now, instead of the slab of polished blackstone they used to bring with them.
highlights: Endless portal rooms scatter extra ways back to the train
Walking back in returns you to the corridor you came out of, not to the start
Some rooms stand their way onward somewhere other than directly opposite
Corridor doorways are built from the room's own walls, not polished blackstone
Portal rooms no longer spill the contents of their bookshelves and chests onto the floor

entries.title: Portal room furnishings are curated, and their mobs scale with difficulty
entries.summary: Furnished portal rooms now draw from a curated set of furnishings instead of anything the train could offer, so a window room reads as a window room. The default portal room's mobs now scale with the run: low difficulties meet zombies, while witches, vindicators and pillagers only start appearing as the difficulty climbs. Furnishings built for portal rooms no longer turn up in ordinary train carriages.
highlights: Portal room mobs scale with difficulty - zombies early, witches and vindicators later
Furnished portal rooms draw from a curated set of furnishings
Portal-only furnishings no longer appear in ordinary carriages
Window portal rooms now use the bedrock-lock layout

entries.title: Portal doorways stay with their carriage instead of being left behind
entries.summary: A portal's doorway belongs to the carriage carrying it. If that carriage was set aside while the train rolled on, the doorway could be left behind hanging where the train used to be — and riding an ordinary carriage through that spot would pull you in and drop you into the empty space beneath the world, without you ever having walked into a portal. A doorway now travels with its carriage or stops existing entirely, and a portal that has nowhere solid on the other side quietly does nothing instead of dropping you.
highlights: Riding an ordinary carriage can no longer pull you through a portal you never walked into
A portal with nowhere solid to land now does nothing rather than dropping you below the world

entries.title: Portals stay out of your opening carriages
entries.summary: Hallway portals no longer turn up in the first stretch of the train. Nothing before difficulty level 2 — around sixty carriages in — holds a portal, so you get to know the train before something that plainly isn't part of it opens up in the middle of it. Past that point portals arrive on their usual sporadic cadence, counted from where they start rather than from the station, so the first one doesn't keep you waiting twice.
highlights: Portals no longer generate before difficulty level 2 (~60 carriages in)
The first portal past that point arrives on the normal cadence, not after a second wait

entries.title: The rooms beyond the corridors count toward your journey, and two new advancements
entries.summary: Step through a carriage corridor into one of the rooms that could never fit inside it and the train keeps rolling without you — but until now, everything you travelled while you were in there counted for nothing. It counts now: you cover as much ground as the train does while you look around. Two new advancements come with it, one for going inside at all, and one for finding your way out somewhere far from where you came in.
highlights: Time and distance now keep counting while you are inside one of the impossible rooms
New advancement: 'Train inside a train?' for stepping out of a corridor into a room that could never have fitted in the carriage
New advancement: 'A new way out' for leaving one of those rooms by a corridor at least 50 blocks from the one you entered through

entries.title: A broken portal can be walked through, and portals stop failing silently
entries.summary: Breaking open a portal corridor's shell still closes the portal for good, but the pair no longer leaves three carriages of dead end behind it: the blocks between its two doors are removed, so you can walk straight through the group and carry on down the train. Separately, a portal you lingered in could quietly stop working — its destination was left behind as the train rolled on, and walking past the midpoint then did nothing at all. It now keeps up with you.
highlights: A severed portal opens into a walk-through instead of a dead end
Portals no longer stop working if you linger in the corridor before crossing

entries.title: Help Translate on the Ways to Help page
entries.summary: If you play Dungeon Train in a language that was machine-translated, the Ways to Help page now offers you the translation editor directly - so fixing the lines that read wrong sits alongside donating, sharing and feedback as a way to help. The page also scrolls now, and its Done button stays put at the bottom instead of sliding off the edge of a small window.
highlights: New "Help Translate" section on the Ways to Help page, shown when your language still has AI-translated lines nobody has reviewed
The Ways to Help page scrolls, and Done is pinned to the bottom so it can never be pushed off-screen

entries.title: Video Tools page for content creators
entries.summary: A new Video Tools button on the title menu, for anyone filming Dungeon Train. Each of the two filming commands gets a tile playing a clip of what it actually looks like — cinematographer mode, which flies you through the train in spectator with every door swinging open ahead of you, and the intro cinematic, which you can replay from anywhere in a run. Click a tile for the full rundown. The page also points you at #streams-and-media-of-dungeontrain to share what you make, and at the dev if you need a hand with a shot.
highlights: New Video Tools page on the title menu, with an animated tile per filming command
/dt cinematographer — spectator flight with auto-opening doors (including on the moving train), an adjustable door radius, and clear-view for shots through walls
/dt cinematic — replay the intro cinematic from anywhere, or press C in spectator
Flags that cinematographer mode puts the run into Free Play, while replaying the cinematic does not
Discord moves to a logomark button above Credits, freeing its old slot for Video Tools

entries.title: Armor stands you place on a train now stay with the train
entries.summary: Placing an armor stand inside a carriage used to look like nothing happened — the stand really was created, but it ended up in the carriage's internal building space rather than on the train you were standing on, where nobody could ever see it. Placed stands now ride the carriage they were put on, staying put as the train moves and surviving a reload.
highlights: Armor stands can be placed and displayed inside carriages
Placed stands stay locked to their carriage while the train moves
They survive carriage unloading and world reload

entries.title: Ride photos for building in a drifting carriage, and for arriving in a Train Dimension
entries.summary: The camera that quietly takes photos of your run now watches for two more moments. Leave your marks on a drifting carriage — somebody else's build that has come to your train — and it takes a photo of the work. Walk a hallway portal and stay a while in the room on the other side, and it takes a wide shot of wherever you have ended up. Both turn up in your gallery and on the death screen with the rest of the run. The Train Dimension photo waits until you have actually walked in and looked around, so it shows the room rather than the doorway, and it is framed to stay inside the room you are standing in rather than the identical one next door.
highlights: New photo taken when you build in a drifting carriage
New photo taken once you have arrived inside a Train Dimension
Train Dimension photos are framed from inside the room you are in, never from the copy next door or from inside a corridor

entries.title: Shorter portal carriages, and a seamless crossing
entries.summary: Portal corridors now come in two lengths. Alongside the long corridor that stretches into the carriage behind it, there is a new one exactly the size of an ordinary carriage — and each portal on the train picks between them, so they no longer all feel the same. Crossing one is smoother too: the door ahead of you is always a real one, changing your mind partway along works, and standing in a doorway never moves you.
highlights: A new carriage-length portal corridor, with its own interior and ten furnishing variants
Roughly half of the portals you meet are the new shorter kind
Change your mind partway along a portal corridor and walk straight back out onto the train
The door in front of you is always one that opens — no more walking into a dead one
Standing in a portal doorway no longer moves you

entries.title: Portal-side carriages hang together
entries.summary: Blocks in the portal-side carriages no longer each pick their own look in isolation — some of them now follow the carriage's stonework, so a run of wall or floor reads as one surface instead of a patchwork. Which blocks follow and which stay independent varies per carriage, so the effect changes as you ride.
highlights: Portal-side contents now share their look between blocks rather than rolling each one separately

entries.title: Train Dimensions: the way back always works
entries.summary: Every corridor in a Train Dimension now takes you back aboard — the one you came in through and the extra ways out scattered deep in the room — however long you stay or how far you wander. Before, a room you had gone far enough into could quietly lose its train, leaving you sealed in with nowhere left to walk.
highlights: Corridor copies deep in an endless room always lead back to the train
No more getting stranded in a Train Dimension you walked too far into
Untested in multiplayer — how this behaves with several players on one train is not yet known

entries.title: Train Dimensions: fixed rooms losing their train
entries.summary: Fixes the way a Train Dimension could lose the carriages it belongs to while you were still inside it, leaving you sealed in a room whose corridors led nowhere. The room now keeps hold of its part of the train for as long as you are in there — and in the unlikely event it loses it anyway, you are put back on the train instead of left with no way out.
highlights: Fixed a room losing its train while you were inside it
Fixed being left with no way out when it happened — you are returned to the train instead
Untested in multiplayer — how this behaves with several players on one train is not yet known

entries.title: Train Dimensions: improvements to the lost-train fix
entries.summary: Improves the recent fix for a Train Dimension losing its train: being put back on board no longer hurts you, and it asks less of the game while it finds the way back.

entries.title: Sealed Train Dimensions are properly sealed
entries.summary: The bedrock around a sealed Train Dimension now covers its hallways and end faces too, instead of stopping at the room — so there is no longer a wall you can mine through to get out.

entries.title: Train Dimension loot now matches its carriage
entries.summary: Chests inside a Train Dimension now roll their loot to the stage of the portal carriage you walked in through, so they're worth what a carriage's chests are worth at that point in the run. Which room you get, and how it is built, is unchanged.
highlights: Train Dimension room loot now scales to the portal carriage you entered from
Enchantment levels in those rooms are capped to the run's progression again

entries.title: Debug command menu is creative-only
entries.summary: The X debug/command menu no longer opens outside creative mode. Shift+X previously bypassed the creative gate and opened it in survival; that override is gone, and the menu now closes itself if you drop out of creative while it is open.
highlights: X and Shift+X no longer open the debug menu in survival
The menu closes automatically when you leave creative

entries.title: Train engine volume slider
entries.summary: The train's engine loop now has its own volume, so you can turn the train down without turning the whole world's ambience down with it. It sits in Options > Music & Sounds beside the other volumes, and is repeated in Options > Dungeon Train and the in-world X menu. Sliding it to OFF stops the engine entirely; everything else about how the sound behaves - loudest in a carriage, fading out as you walk away, quiet in a Train Dimension room - is unchanged, just quieter or louder overall.
highlights: New Dungeon Train Engine volume slider in Options > Music & Sounds
Separate from the Ambient slider, so cave and mob sounds keep their own level
OFF silences the engine completely

entries.title: The train tells you when a book went unsigned
entries.summary: Shelve a book & quill you wrote in but never signed, and a quiet line tells you the train won't carry it. Signing is what sends a book out into the world — an unsigned one just sits on the shelf, and now the game says so instead of leaving you guessing.
highlights: Putting a written-in but unsigned book & quill into a chiseled bookshelf shows one of five lines
Nothing else changes: the book still goes on the shelf and can be taken back out

entries.title: The house — a player-built room
entries.summary: Built in the Train Editor by Twitch streamer xxx606xxx_, and the first player-made package to ship with Dungeon Train.

entries.title: Portal rooms can be one author's library
entries.summary: A portal room can now be a single community author's library. Its bookshelves are stocked with that person's whole catalogue and every shelf past the end of it is left empty, so a hall of bare shelves with a dozen books in it tells you exactly how much they wrote. The room announces whose library you have walked into.
highlights: New Books setting on portal rooms in the editor: off, or an author mix.
The room rolls between your own writing and somebody else's, and each room sets its own odds — a study can lean toward your own shelves while a great hall leans toward strangers.
Rooms can ask for a particular kind of author: at least this many books written, and at most that many, so a modest private collection stays modest.
Written nothing yourself? The room quietly picks somebody else rather than standing empty.

entries.title: Two new Train Dimension rooms
entries.summary: Two more rooms can turn up behind a Train Dimension portal. One is a trap room, sealed on every side in bedrock. The other is a parkour room with nothing around it at all - no walls, no shell, just empty space out past the fog. Both start showing up from level 10, and both are uncommon, so the rooms you already know still make up most of what you walk into.
highlights: New trap room, sealed all the way round in bedrock
New parkour room, hanging in open space with no shell around it
Both appear from level 10 onward

entries.title: New dimensional carriages by Lil Detective Crunch
entries.summary: Two new dimensional carriages built by Lil Detective Crunch now ride the train, one of them stocked with nether-themed loot and mobs.
highlights: Two new dimensional carriages by Lil Detective Crunch

entries.title: Nether lava fix
entries.summary: Lava in the Nether band now behaves the way it should.

entries.title: Better review for player translation fixes
entries.summary: When you correct a machine-translated string in the in-game translation editor, your client now also reports the AI text you replaced. The reviewer sees your fix side by side with the original instead of on its own, so genuine corrections are easier to tell apart and quicker to approve.

entries.title: Saving in the editor no longer re-mirrors your build
entries.summary: Hitting Save in an in-game editor used to rebuild the mirrored half of the plot from the master octant first, quietly overwriting anything you had deliberately made asymmetric — and anything placed by a route the live mirror doesn't watch, like a clipboard paste or an edit made before you turned the axis on. Save now captures the plot exactly as you left it. When you do want the far half rebuilt from the master, ask for it: the new Mirror -> Rebuild button in the editor menu, or /dungeontrain editor mirror rebuild.
highlights: Save captures the plot as it stands — mirroring no longer runs behind your back
New on-demand re-mirror: Mirror -> Rebuild in the editor menu, or /dungeontrain editor mirror rebuild
Live mirroring while you build is unchanged

entries.title: Fortresses and bastions in the Nether
entries.summary: The Nether crossing is no longer empty country. Nether fortresses, bastion remnants, nether fossils and ruined portals now generate out there — the real ones, with their own loot, their blaze spawners and wither skeleton halls, their piglin brutes and Pigstep. Fortresses stand on their own bridge supports over the lava, and where one happens to lie across the line, the train tunnels straight through it.
highlights: Nether fortresses generate in the Nether crossing, with blazes, wither skeletons and their loot
Bastion remnants, complete with piglin brutes, treasure rooms and the netherite upgrade template
Nether fossils in soul sand valleys, and ruined portals with their blackstone and loot
Ride straight through a fortress that lands across the tracks

entries.title: Effortless Building now bundled in the modpack (off by default)
entries.summary: The Dungeon Train modpack now ships Effortless Building alongside the rest of the pack, switched off. Flip it on in the launcher's mod list if you want its building tools — multi-block placement, mirrors and arrays — while you build out your train.
highlights: Effortless Building included in the pack, disabled by default — one click to enable

entries.title: Dimensional carriages can be built up to 80 blocks tall
entries.summary: The room inside a dimensional carriage was capped at 11 blocks tall. It can now be built up to 80.

entries.title: Portal room chests no longer hold gear with impossible stats
entries.summary: A Train Dimension room could hand you gear with absurd stat values — a diamond chestplate with over four million armour. The items were stored inside the room itself, so they turned up for everyone who found that chest. Affected rooms are repaired, and any room still holding such an item now rolls it again at the difficulty of where you found it, so it arrives as ordinary loot. Gear you find deep in a run still scales exactly as it did.
highlights: Fixed a Train Dimension room that held gear with impossible stat values
Rooms still holding such an item now reroll it as ordinary loot
Items can no longer be generated with impossible stats in the first place

entries.title: New supporter names and the Archivist
entries.summary: Twelve more Discord supporters join the item name pool, along with the Archivist Society and Archivist and Detective titles.
highlights: Requires Adventure Item Names 0.48.0

entries.title: Nether band mobs no longer spawn in dimensional carriages
entries.summary: Ghasts, zombified piglins and magma cubes could spawn inside a dimensional carriage while the train crossed the Nether band. They no longer do.

entries.title: Drifting-carriage messages no longer flood chat
entries.summary: Walking a run of drifting carriages used to fill chat with a new gray line every few seconds. Those messages are now capped at three per ten seconds, so the train still tells you when you have stepped into someone else's carriage without burying everything else you were reading.
highlights: Drifting-carriage entry messages capped at 3 per 10 seconds

entries.title: Crops saved into carriage templates stay planted
entries.summary: Wheat, carrots, potatoes and beetroot saved into a carriage template no longer break the moment the carriage appears — farm carriages now ride the train intact. Crops inside a carriage no longer need light to stay planted, so an unlit farm carriage keeps its crops at the age you saved them. They still need light to grow, and still need farmland underneath: break the soil and the crop pops just like anywhere else. Also fixes saved crops vanishing from the carriage editor when you reopened a template.
highlights: Wheat and other crops saved into carriage templates stay planted
Crops in an unlit carriage keep their saved growth stage (they still need light to grow)
Crops no longer vanish from a template when reopened in the carriage editor

entries.title: End city adjustments
entries.summary: End city adjustments.
highlights: End city adjustments.

entries.title: More skies for dimensions
entries.summary: New sky options for dimensions.

entries.title: Fewer trivial runs in the passenger log
entries.summary: The public passenger log now only carries runs that got somewhere. A run that ends before carriage 100 stays off the feed — whether you died, quit, or abandoned it — so the log fills with journeys instead of false starts. The one exception: if another player's echo strikes you down, your run is posted however early it happened.
highlights: Runs ending before carriage 100 no longer post to the public passenger log
Being killed by an echo always posts, at any carriage count

entries.title: Improving dimensional carriages in the Upside Down
entries.summary: Improving dimensional carriages in the Upside Down.

entries.title: Six player-built portal rooms
entries.summary: Six new portal rooms, designed and built by players in the in-game editor — thanks to Autistic Mime, General Efficiency and Lil Detective Crunch. Which one you find depends on how far down the line you are, so the further you ride the stranger they get.
highlights: Built by Autistic Mime, General Efficiency and Lil Detective Crunch
Six new rooms, each gated by distance
New loot: an End-themed chest, a gambling chest, and a mixed-blocks chest
Their chests were rebuilt clean — the authors' worlds had baked in gear with impossible stats

entries.title: Water and lava in carriages
entries.summary: Carriages can now feature water and lava. Train builders can drop a liquid into a block variant, so a carriage might roll a flooded floor, a lava channel, or stay dry — and the liquid always arrives as a proper source block rather than a puddle that drains away.
highlights: Water and lava can be used as block variants in carriages.
Liquids always place as full source blocks, so they don't drain away.

entries.title: Sky block and portal room tweaks
entries.summary: Small adjustments to sky blocks and portal rooms.

entries.title: Edible Backpacks
entries.summary: Apple packs now turn up in train loot. Eat one and you gain an extra backpack slot for the rest of your run — storage that lives in two panels either side of your inventory screen, growing a column at a time as you eat more. Golden apple packs are worth nine slots in a single bite, and nine ordinary packs craft into one. Die and the backpack goes with you, space and all, so what you carry in it is a real bet.
highlights: Eat an apple pack for an extra inventory slot that lasts the rest of your run (up to 108)
Storage panels sit either side of the inventory screen and hide with the recipe book
Golden apple packs grant nine slots at once; craft one from nine ordinary packs
Dying costs you the backpack: both its contents and the space itself

entries.title: Three more supporter names
entries.summary: Three more Discord supporters join the item name pool: mel, banguela, and morpheus the 3 feeted cat.
highlights: Adventure Item Names 0.49.0 adds the new names — 0.48.0 still works, it just never rolls them

entries.title: Refill the Trade Anything slot with one key
entries.summary: Updated the bundled Trade Everything mod. Tap space over a villager's Trade Anything slot to top it back up from your inventory instead of dragging stacks in one at a time, and obsidian now has a set trade value.
highlights: Space-bar refill for the Trade Anything slot
Obsidian trades at 4 per emerald

entries.title: clientcommands counts as a cheat mod
entries.summary: Playing with clientcommands installed now puts the session into Free Play.

entries.title: Tectonic removed from the modpack
entries.summary: The modpack no longer bundles Tectonic or Lithostitched. Dungeon Train still works with Tectonic if you install it yourself; if you had it switched on, it goes away on your next pack update.

entries.title: Seven new advancements
entries.summary: Three chase the bundled Edible Backpacks: eat one, craft the compressed nine-slot version, then unlock every backpack slot there is. Two reward riding past 100 and 1,000 carriages without opening a single chest or barrel (vases don't count). One is granted when you die more than 1,000 carriages into a life that never touched an ender chest. And one is for finding the train engine volume slider.
highlights: Apples? / Hungry for Apples / Got Apples — the edible backpack chain
Not My Chest / Still Not My Chest — 100 and 1,000 carriages without looting a chest or barrel
Contained Loop — a 1,000+ carriage life that never opened an ender chest
Sound Check — change the train engine volume

entries.title: Rave room
entries.summary: A new carriage room stocked with music discs — the full vanilla set, occasionally worn or enchanted.

entries.title: Drifting carriages remember who died in them
entries.summary: A drifting carriage already tells you a little about itself when you step aboard — that somebody built it, and who. It now tells you one more thing: who died in it. These are real deaths, in other people's runs, in worlds you will never see; the carriage carried the fact along with the build. A carriage nobody has died in says nothing at all, which makes the ones that do speak worth reading.
highlights: Stepping into a drifting carriage names the travellers whose runs ended there
The death log travels with the build, so it reaches you from other players' worlds
Deaths by players who have not shared their name are counted, never named

entries.title: Shared carriages bring their furnishings with them
entries.summary: A community carriage used to travel as bare blocks: the armor stands, item frames, paintings and animals someone decorated their room with were left behind when the build shipped to another world. Now they come too — a shared carriage arrives furnished, exactly as its builder left it.
highlights: Armor stands, item frames, paintings, end crystals and mobs inside a shared carriage are saved with the build and placed back when another world receives it.
They ride the moving train with the carriage, rather than being left standing on the tracks.
The carriage browser's 3D preview now shows them, labelled by type and custom name, with a toggle to hide the labels.
Server owners can cap how many travel per carriage (sharedCarriageMaxEntities, default 64) or turn the whole thing off with 0.

entries.title: Emerald blocks trade at their real value
entries.summary: Villagers could hand you a whole emerald block (worth 9 emeralds) for a stack of cheap goods once their trade list included an emerald-block price. The Trade Anything slot now treats emerald blocks as currency rather than tradeable goods, and pays out in emeralds when a payout block would be worth more than everything you put in. Genuinely valuable items — netherite gear and the like — still pay out in blocks.
highlights: A stack of wheat now pays out in emeralds instead of minting an emerald block.
High-value items still pay out in emerald blocks, at nine emeralds per block.

entries.title: Nemo's Inventory Sorting available in the modpack
entries.summary: The Dungeon Train modpack now offers Nemo's Inventory Sorting as an optional add-on. Turn it on in the launcher's optional-mods list to get one-click sort buttons on your inventory and any chest — handy when a loot run leaves your carriage storage a mess. It's off by default, so nothing changes unless you opt in.
highlights: New opt-in companion mod: Nemo's Inventory Sorting (client-side, 1.8.2.1)
Adds sort buttons to inventory and container screens
Ships switched off — enable it in the launcher's optional mods list

entries.title: Punchy! now in the modpack (off by default)
entries.summary: The Dungeon Train modpack now ships Punchy!, a first-person animation mod that adds weight and personality to swinging, mining and movement. It's included but switched off — flip it on in your launcher's mod list if you want it.
highlights: Punchy! 2.7d bundled in both the CurseForge and Modrinth packs
Disabled by default — enable it with one click, no extra download
Client-side only, so it's skipped on dedicated servers

entries.title: Edible backpacks are rarer
entries.summary: The edible backpack turned up in almost every other chest. Its odds are now cut across the general, iron/gold and pot loot pools, and it no longer appears in the starter chest — so finding one feels like a find again.
highlights: Edible backpack far less common in chests
No longer handed out in the starter chest

entries.title: Miniword — a new House portal room
entries.summary: Step through a portal into Miniword, a hand-built world in a box and by far the largest portal room in the game at 48x30x48. It turns up as a House room from Diff-Level 12 onward.
highlights: New Miniword portal room — a 48x30x48 build, the biggest room in Dungeon Train
Appears among the House portal rooms from Diff-Level 12

entries.title: Vein miner mods now trigger Free Play
entries.summary: Playing with a vein miner installed runs the session in Free Play.

entries.title: Difficulty changes now ask first
entries.summary: Changing difficulty swaps your gear, XP and Ender Chest. It now warns you before it does — and the gear you leave behind is no longer lost.

entries.title: Trade Everything is now its own download
entries.summary: Trade Everything — the mod that gives every villager a "Trade Anything" slot — used to ride along inside Dungeon Train's own file. It now installs alongside Dungeon Train as its own mod, so it shows up in your mod list and gets credited for its own downloads. The CurseForge and Modrinth apps fetch it for you automatically; if you install by hand, grab Trade Everything (0.7.0 or newer) with Dungeon Train.
highlights: The CurseForge and Modrinth apps install Trade Everything for you — nothing to do.
Installing manually? Add Trade Everything 0.7.0+ next to Dungeon Train, or the game will tell you it's missing on launch.
Villager payouts fixed: selling no longer hands back emerald blocks priced as ordinary goods.
Bookshelves are now valued at 3 per emerald.

entries.title: Immediate Respawn now rolls straight into a new run
entries.summary: Turn on Minecraft's Immediate Respawn game rule and dying skips the death screen entirely — the world is discarded and a fresh Dungeon Train run starts on the spot, the same reboard the death screen's "Board anew" button performs. Previously the rule dropped you back into the world you had just died in, the one way a run could outlive your death. Multiplayer is unchanged: on a server you do not host, Immediate Respawn still respawns you as vanilla does.
highlights: Immediate Respawn ends the run and starts a new world, no button press
Holding Shift while you die keeps the current game mode, as on the reboard chip
Remote servers keep vanilla Immediate Respawn behaviour

entries.title: Edible backpacks come from loot tables only
entries.summary: Edible backpacks were being swapped into 1.5% of every loot slot in the game, on top of the chests and pots that were meant to carry them. That global substitution is gone — backpacks now turn up only where the loot tables actually list them, so finding one means something again.
highlights: Edible backpacks no longer replace random items in unrelated containers
Backpacks still appear in the loot chests, iron/gold chests and decorated pots that list them

entries.title: Community books can't break your game — and can still be styled
entries.summary: Books written by other players are now cleaned up before they reach you. Certain characters could previously hide text on a page or stack accent marks until it overflowed, and an emoji landing in exactly the wrong spot in a long title could crash the game outright. That's all handled now, on the server and in the mod. Colour codes and right-to-left writing still work exactly as they did — the cleanup is aimed at characters that do nothing but cause trouble. Ordinary books are unaffected.
highlights: Colour and style codes still work in your book's pages — they're only stripped from titles and author names, where they leaked out into chat and tooltips
Invisible padding characters are removed from titles, authors and pages; right-to-left writing and emoji sequences are left alone
An emoji in a long title or a full page can no longer crash the game
Books already in the community pool are cleaned as they're handed out — nothing needed re-uploading

entries.title: Report a community book
entries.summary: Community books written by other players now carry a report button beside the thumbs up and down. A thumbs down says a book was weak; reporting says it should not be in the pool at all. Enough reports, relative to how many people have read it, pull the book from circulation and put it in front of a human.
highlights: A report icon sits under the thumbs on the train's question page, on player-written books only
It takes two clicks — the first arms it, the second sends — and there is no hotkey, so a slip cannot report a book
Reporting does not cast a vote; the two are separate verdicts
Reports are weighed against readers, so a well-read book is not pulled by a handful of complaints

entries.title: Open-plain portal rooms can vary their floor
entries.summary: Endless Open portal rooms can now reroll their floor and ceiling per tile instead of repeating one pattern to the horizon.

entries.title: WorldEdit available in the modpack
entries.summary: The modpack now ships WorldEdit as an optional extra. It's switched off by default — tick it on in the launcher's optional-mods list if you want an in-game map editor for building. Best used off the moving train: WorldEdit's block edits aren't aware of the train's physics sub-level.
highlights: WorldEdit bundled in the modpack, off by default
Enable it from the optional-mods list in the CurseForge/Modrinth launcher

entries.title: Using a creative mod asks first
entries.summary: Using WorldEdit or Effortless Building now asks whether you want to enter Free Play, the same way switching to Creative does. Decline and nothing happens. Having them installed changes nothing on its own.
highlights: Ordinary building with Effortless Building is still normal play

entries.title: Villager trade tweaks
entries.summary: Adjusted what villagers pay for a few items in the Trade Anything slot.

entries.title: Player heads remember who died there
entries.summary: The player heads scattered through the train are no longer anonymous. Each one now wears the face and name of a real player whose run ended at that same carriage — the fourth carriage remembers people who fell in a fourth carriage. Mine one and the head keeps them, so you can carry a fallen traveller with you or set them up somewhere of your choosing.
highlights: Heads in carriage N show players who died at carriage N
A mined head keeps its face and name, and can be placed anywhere
Falls back to the bundled skins when there is nobody to remember yet

entries.title: Portal corridor loot variety
entries.summary: Chests in a portal's corridors now roll different contents from portal to portal, instead of the same ones every time.

entries.title: Bilibili link for Chinese-language players
entries.summary: Playing in Chinese? There's now a Bilibili button on the main menu, just above Discord — Discord doesn't work in mainland China, so that one was a dead end. It only shows up on Chinese-language clients; everyone else's menu is unchanged.
highlights: New Bilibili button on the main menu, above Discord
Shows only on Chinese-language clients (简体中文, 繁體中文, 文言文)
Discord stays where it is — the Bilibili link is added, not swapped in

entries.title: Endless Open rooms can repeat a single block variant
entries.summary: An endless open portal room can now be set to repeat one block instead of the room you arrived in — an open plain of sandstone, or of a mix you build yourself. The room you walk into keeps everything its author built; only the ground stretching away from it goes uniform. The block can be a full block variant, with weights, facings and even gaps, authored in the same block-variant menu the rest of the editor uses.
highlights: Copies: a new Single option for Endless Open rooms
Repeat one block, or a whole block variant with weights and facings
Air in the variant leaves gaps in the plain
The default portal room now opens onto a lit plain of shroomlight and blackstone

entries.title: Reviewers can reply to translators, and translators can retire good AI lines
entries.summary: The in-game translation editor now carries a conversation. When a reviewer turns down a translation you sent, they can say why — and that reply comes back to your client, marked against the line it is about, readable in the list and above the box when you open it, with a note on the title screen when something new is waiting. And when a machine-translated line is already correct, you can now say so: 'Good As Is' retires it from your queue so it stops coming back, and you can put it back at any time.
highlights: Reviewers can reply to a translation, and the reply reaches the translator's client
A title-screen note tells you when a reviewer has written back
'Good As Is' retires a machine-translated line that needs no fixing — reversible, and per install

entries.title: CurseForge modpack keeps up with releases again
entries.summary: The CurseForge modpack had quietly stopped updating — it sat on v0.592.0 while the mod shipped v0.613.0, because CurseForge was accepting our uploads and then rejecting them behind the scenes with no error anywhere we could see. Uploads now retry when the platform hiccups, and every upload is checked afterwards to confirm it actually went live, so the pack can't silently fall behind again.
highlights: CurseForge modpack is publishing again
Failed uploads retry instead of losing that version
A pack version that never goes live now fails loudly

entries.title: Three weeks of new text, now in all 19 languages
entries.summary: Everything added since early August was English-only outside en_us — the seven new advancements, the Video Tools page, the skybox blocks, the difficulty-change warning, the drifting-carriage death lines, the community-book report button and more. All of it is now translated into every language Dungeon Train ships in, along with ten in-world books that had never been localized. Machine-translated and marked as such, so the in-game translation editor lists them for human review.
highlights: 115 newly translated interface lines in each of the 19 languages
Ten new books — including The Drifting Carriages and the cursed and loved starting books — now read in your language
New Quiet Rules and Train Glossary entries translated to match the English originals

entries.title: JEI, ready to switch on
entries.summary: The modpack now ships Just Enough Items, off by default. Tick it on at install for recipe and item lookup — press R on any item to see how it's made.
highlights: Bundled with the modpack, switched off by default.

entries.title: Undo and redo in the train editor
entries.summary: The in-world editor now has an undo history on Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y (Cmd+Z / Cmd+Y on Mac), with an Undo | Redo row in the editor's X menu. It covers block edits, whole-plot actions like Clear and Reset, block variants, and menu changes such as weights, stage links, loot tables and part assignments. Undo works from anywhere — change something, walk away, and you can still take it back.
highlights: Ctrl/Cmd+Z and Ctrl/Cmd+Y, rebindable from the vanilla Controls screen
Blocks, whole-plot Clear and Reset, block variants, and menu changes all undo
A mirrored edit undoes as one step, not one per reflected cell
Broken containers come back with their contents intact
Works from anywhere, not just while standing in the plot

entries.title: Sable updated to 2.0.5
entries.summary: Dungeon Train now runs on Sable 2.0.5, which fixes several upstream crashes — most notably a panic when you close the CurseForge or Modrinth launcher before entering a world. Sable is a required download, so update it too.
highlights: Fixes the crash from closing the launcher before joining a world
Requires Sable 2.0.5 — the modpack updates it for you

entries.title: Carriages no longer shift when their blocks change
entries.summary: Blowing up or mining blocks on a carriage could shove the whole carriage sideways, and the shift survived a save and reload. Beds in the Nether and End were the loudest case, but creepers, trap TNT and ordinary mining did it too.

entries.title: Endless plains can have a different floor and roof
entries.summary: A repeating plain's floor and roof are now set separately in the editor, and either one can be air.

entries.title: The deserter's hall by MacaroniWithTheMayonnaise
entries.summary: A new portal room behind house doors: a spruce hall built by MacaroniWithTheMayonnaise, with the deserter's journal still inside.
highlights: Built by MacaroniWithTheMayonnaise

entries.title: Edible backpacks are findable again
entries.summary: Edible backpacks turn up in loot chests, iron/gold chests, decorated pots and the starter chest at their original rates again.

entries.title: Dimensional carriages can stand under their own sky
entries.summary: A dimensional carriage's template now chooses the sky it stands under — ordinary daylight, daylight that follows the world clock, or a Nether or End cast. The light eases in as you step inside and eases back out as you leave for the corridor home. The mini-world carriage is the first to use it.
highlights: The mini-world dimensional carriage is now daylit
Room builders get a Sky control in the dimensional carriage editor
Turn it off server-wide with the new portalRoomDaylight setting

entries.title: Version number now shown on the pause menu
entries.summary: The Dungeon Train version line that sits in the corner of the main menu now also appears on the pause menu, so you can check which build you are on without leaving your run. It carries the same update notice as the title screen — if a newer release is out, the line turns amber and clicking it opens the download page for wherever you installed the mod.
highlights: Version number added to the pause (Esc) menu, matching the main menu
Shows the same clickable 'update available' notice as the title screen
Visible in multiplayer as well as singleplayer

entries.title: Endless portal rooms no longer vanish under other players
entries.summary: In multiplayer, the endless portal rooms only followed one player — usually the host. Anyone else could watch the floor disappear from around them and drop out of the world, and the room stopped growing ahead of them. Every player in the room now gets their own window of rooms.
highlights: The floor around you is never cleared while you are standing near it, whoever else is in the room
The room keeps building ahead of every player exploring it, not just the first one in
Extra corridors are held open the same way, so the way back does not disappear behind you

entries.title: Flag a cheat mod from the death screen
entries.summary: The Mod Recommendations page now works both ways. Alongside recommending a mod to the creator, each of your installed mods carries a small warning icon — click it to flag that mod as a cheat or hack, say what it lets you do, and send. Flagged mods sink to the bottom of the grid with a warning mark, the way recommended ones keep their tick.
highlights: Report any installed mod as a cheat or hack, with a reason
Recommendations are unchanged — the tile body still recommends

entries.title: Changed settings now show at launch, with one-click restore
entries.summary: Dungeon Train's difficulty settings are what your advancements and lifetime stats are measured against, so a world running with them changed now plays in Free Play — the same rule that already applied to Adventure Item Stats. If your settings differ, the game tells you on the title screen, lists exactly what changed, and offers to put them back. Your own settings are always backed up first, never deleted, so you can rename a file back to restore them. Settings that don't affect balance — visual options, Discord and telemetry toggles, and the content filters — are unaffected.
highlights: Changed difficulty settings are shown at launch, not discovered mid-run
One-click restore to defaults, with your old settings kept as backups
Keeping your changes is remembered, so you're only asked again if something else changes
New /fixconfig command does the same restore from in-game

entries.title: Find the books you wrote, even the ones the train hasn't let out
entries.summary: Your own library rooms now stock the books you wrote that the train is still deciding about — or has decided against. Open one and its last page tells you where it stands, in the train's own words. You can also take one of your released books back out of circulation whenever you like.
highlights: Books you wrote that are pending, undecided or refused now appear on your own library shelves instead of vanishing the moment you sign them.
The last page of one of your books says where it stands: still being read, undecided, or turned away — in orange, or red once it is a no.
Made Private: take one of your released books off the line so only you can find it. Reversible — the padlock shows what it will do before you click it.
Protest a verdict you disagree with, on a book the train has actually read. It asks a person to look again; it does not overturn anything by itself.
No thumbs on a book you wrote — rating your own work was never the point, and it skewed which books everyone else was shown.

entries.title: See how your own books are landing
entries.summary: The last page of a book you wrote now shows its thumbs up and thumbs down count. The numbers refresh whenever you pick the book up.
highlights: Vote counts sit where the voting buttons are on other people's books — yours report, they don't ask.
A released book of yours shows its tally even at zero, so "nobody has voted yet" is something you can actually see.

entries.title: Portal room variety restored
entries.summary: Since v0.630.0 portal rooms had been coming up as libraries far more often than intended, and those libraries always drew from your own shelf instead of mixing in other writers. Test settings had been shipped as real content by mistake. The original room weights are back.
highlights: Libraries are rare again, and the rooms you meet are varied again.
Library rooms go back to mostly showing other people's writing, with your own as the occasional treat.

entries.title: Custom train content now asks before it changes your run
entries.summary: If you've built your own carriages in the Train Editor — or installed someone else's pack — starting a world now asks what you want to do with them. Continue and you play with your creations, but the run counts as Free Play: it won't add to your profile or global stats. Disable them and the world runs the built-in designs, and your stats count as normal. Tick 'Remember decision' and it won't ask again; you can change your mind any time in Options, or with /customcontent.
highlights: A prompt at the start of any world running custom train content, with Continue / Disable Custom Changes and a Remember decision checkbox.
Playing with custom content is Free Play — advancements still earn live, but they don't count towards your profile or global totals.
Disabling is per-world and reversible: the world falls back to the built-in designs, and /customcontent on brings yours back.
A new Custom Train Content row in Options -> Dungeon Train sets what happens by default.

entries.title: Move, turn and mirror a whole template in the editor
entries.summary: The train editor can now rearrange the plot you are standing in, instead of you rebuilding it block by block. Offset slides the build and wraps it at the plot edges, rotate turns it, and flip mirrors it — and any of the three is a single Ctrl+Z away from being undone.
highlights: /dt editor offset <x> <y> <z> slides the build, wrapping at the plot faces so nothing is lost
/dt editor rotate 90|180|270 turns the build; a quarter turn needs a square plot, so carriages take 180
/dt editor flip x|y|z mirrors the build, vertical flips included
Variant pools, lock groups and container loot pools travel with the blocks — the build stays wired up

entries.title: Blocks left outside a template plot show up red
entries.summary: Only what sits inside a plot is saved into the template. Anything outside it now wears a red ghost, from anywhere in the editor.

entries.title: Reset your progress
entries.summary: A Reset Everything button on the Video Tools page. Wipes your advancements, stats, story progress, Ender Chest and past lives, and deletes your Dungeon Train worlds, so the game treats you as a first-time player again.
highlights: Names every world it will delete and makes you type DELETE first — there is no undo
Worlds without Dungeon Train in them are left alone

entries.title: Dimensional carriage libraries follow your network-access choice
entries.summary: A dimensional carriage that stocks its shelves from your own writing has to ask the server which books are yours, which means sending your player ID. It now does that only if you allowed network access; if you declined, the carriage stocks from another player's library instead.

entries.title: Translation editor keeps your search, and its scrollbars work
entries.summary: Opening a string in the translation editor no longer wipes what you typed in the search box or your place in the list — both are still there when you come back. The editor's two lists also have working scrollbars now: clicking or dragging the bar scrolls, instead of selecting the row hiding behind it.
highlights: Search text and scroll position survive opening a string
Scrollbars are clickable and draggable in both the strings list and the sent column

entries.title: Dimensional carriages, and more of them in Creative
entries.summary: The room between a portal's two corridors is now called a dimensional carriage in-game, matching what the notes have been calling it. In Creative they arrive on an exact beat — every 5 carriage groups — instead of at random, so you always know where the next one is. Survival is unchanged. Set the rate for a world with /dungeontrain portal carriage <n>; doing so puts the world into Free Play.

entries.title: Library rooms stock authors you can read
entries.summary: A library portal room fills its shelves with one community author's whole catalogue — and now it only ever picks somebody writing in your game's language. Play in 中文 and the room is a Chinese author's library; play in English and it is an English one. When nobody writes in your language yet, the room falls back to an English author rather than standing empty.
highlights: Author libraries are chosen in your language, not just filtered afterwards
The book count on the room's author is now the count in your language
Your own library room still shows everything you have written, in any language

entries.title: Modpack releases stop silently going missing from CurseForge
entries.summary: The CurseForge modpack is published from a manifest that points at that release's Dungeon Train file. If CurseForge has not approved that file yet, it rejects the whole pack — quietly, after the upload looked fine. The release pipeline now waits for the file to actually be approved before building the pack, and stops with a clear reason if it never is, instead of shipping nothing and reporting success.
highlights: Pack uploads no longer reference an unapproved mod file
A stuck release fails loudly instead of going silently missing

entries.title: Find your language, and ask for one that isn't there
entries.summary: The language list has a search box and a filter, every language can now be translated instead of only the nineteen we ship, and translators who volunteered since the last release are named in the credits.
highlights: Search the language list by name, by country, or by locale code — in your own language or in English. "French", "Französisch", "Germany" and "Switzerland" all find what you would expect, and one country brings up every language spoken there.
A filter beside the search: all languages, ones with machine translation still waiting on a human, ones a person has been through, and ones with no translation at all.

The translation editor opens on ANY language, not just the ones Dungeon Train ships. Every line is listed, blank where nothing has been translated yet — including book prose, which was previously invisible if a language had never touched it.
No machine translation for your language? A button asks for one, and shows how many other players have asked for the same.
Credits now name every translator whose work has been approved, not only those whose work had shipped when the build was made.

entries.title: Numbers read correctly in languages that decline them
entries.summary: Counts in chat and on the death screen now take the grammatical form your language actually wants. Russian says «1 раз», «2 раза», «5 раз» instead of forcing everything into one of two English shapes, and the death-screen epitaph reads «второй, кто пал» rather than «два-й». English was quietly wrong here too — it used to say "the twoth to fall". Languages that don't inflect for number, like Japanese and Chinese, are unaffected.
highlights: Russian and Polish counts decline properly — one, few and many forms, including the teens and the second decade
Death-screen epitaphs spell real ordinals: «второй, кто пал», "the second to fall"
Elapsed times, book stats, and shared-carriage death lines all follow the reader's own language

entries.title: Saving a train package no longer loses your work
entries.summary: Saving in the Train Editor's Packages menu is now purely additive — it never deletes or moves anything you have built. Edits you make after saving a package now land in that package, so they stick.
highlights: Saving under a new name makes a copy; the package you saved from stays exactly where it was, along with its .zip snapshot.
Your first save copies your in-progress work into the new package instead of moving it, leaving the originals in place as a backup.
Portal room, tunnel, track and pillar edits — including removing a block variant — are now written into the package you have active, instead of silently going somewhere the game was not reading.
Saving over a package name that only exists as a .zip is now refused rather than overwriting that .zip.
If a save cannot finish, your previous snapshot is left untouched instead of being deleted first.
The Packages menu now shows Save only on the active package's row, so it can no longer look like it will save a different one.
The custom train content prompt no longer appears when your run is already Free Play, where it had nothing left to ask.

entries.title: Hand-written lore books can be stocked in train loot chests
entries.summary: Books written and signed inside an editor plot are now ordinary written books while you build with them — they no longer catch fire when you read or drop them, so you can proof-read one and place it in a carriage's chest. Once that carriage rides the live train, the first player to take the book out of the chest arms it, and it burns after being read like any other book you find out there.
highlights: Books signed in an editor plot no longer burn while you're building
Authored books can be stocked in a carriage's loot chest and saved into the template
Found on the live train, they still burn after reading

entries.title: Better book writing
entries.summary: Writing a book in-game is far less painful. The Dungeon Train modpack now bundles Scribble, which adds page insert and delete, undo and redo, and the ability to save a book to a file and load it back later. Books you write still look exactly the same to everyone else, whether or not they have the mod.
highlights: Insert and delete pages anywhere in a book, instead of only adding to the end
Undo and redo while writing
Save a book to a file and load it back into a fresh book and quill
Scribble's colour picker is switched off, so book text stays vanilla black — set colorPickerVisible in your Dungeon Train client config to bring it back

entries.title: Every animal you tame is counted in your death report
entries.summary: Tame a wolf, a cat, a horse — anything — and it is tallied for the life you are living. When that life ends, the count appears on your death screen and in your death report alongside the rest of the run: how far you got, what you fought, what you carried. A life spent making friends of animals now leaves a mark in the record, not just in the moment.
highlights: Taming anything counts toward the life you are currently living, and resets when you die.
The tally shows on the in-game death screen and in the Discord death report.

entries.title: Your pets come back with your echo
entries.summary: The animals you tamed are remembered when you die. When an echo of that life returns to the train, up to three of your pets walk back on with it — loyal to the echo exactly as they were to you. They follow it down the carriage, teleport to it when they fall behind, and turn on anyone who attacks it. Mounts stay behind unless you gave them a name: a horse you never named was transport, not a companion.
highlights: Up to three tamed animals return alongside an echo of the life that tamed them.
They follow, teleport and defend exactly as pets do for a living player.
Unnamed mounts are left behind; a named one comes back with you.
Taming counts as kindness, so a life spent befriending animals returns friendlier.
Requires Interactive Player Mobs 0.92.0 or newer.

entries.title: Only dimensional carriages take you to their rooms
entries.summary: An ordinary carriage could send you into a dimensional carriage's room without you ever walking through one. It no longer can.

entries.title: The train refuses a book you have already sent
entries.summary: Send the train the same book twice and it now says no, and stops taking your writing for a while — thirty seconds the first time, doubling with each repeat, up to an hour. While it is refusing you, the Sign button in the book screen turns red and will not press, with the time left on it, so you never burn a book for nothing. Someone else writing out a book they found in loot is not affected: only re-sending your OWN book counts.
highlights: A re-upload of your own book is refused instead of silently ignored
Uploads pause for 30s, doubling per repeat, capped at an hour and forgotten after a clean week
The Sign button goes red and dead while paused, and frees itself when the time is up
Lectern letters, Death Notes and Love Notes are all paused too

entries.title: A cat rides the train, and netherite scrap turns up in loot
entries.summary: Carriages that carried cows may now carry a cat instead — or, rarely, an ocelot. Netherite scrap has also been added to the loot tables.
highlights: New cat carriage content, with a rare ocelot variant
Netherite scrap added to prefab loot

entries.title: A book the train never confirmed is no longer counted twice
entries.summary: If the train stored your book but the reply never got back to you — a restart, a timeout, a bad connection — your game sends it again, as it always has. That resend was being read as you uploading the same book twice, and it briefly cost four writers an upload pause they had not earned. Each upload now carries a handle the train recognises, so a resend is understood as the same book arriving again rather than a new offence.
highlights: A re-sent upload is recognised as a retry and never counts as a duplicate

entries.title: Choose your train before the world starts
entries.summary: If you've made your own train designs, Dungeon Train now asks what you want to do the moment you start a run — not after the world has already been built around the answer. Pick Custom Train to play your designs, or Default Train to play the built-in ones with your stats counting as normal.
highlights: The question is asked when you press New World or reboard, so choosing Default Train means a world that never loads the custom content at all.
Two clear cards instead of a wall of text, with a ? button explaining what Free Play costs.
The Free Play badge no longer lingers on saves where it no longer applies — it clears itself on your next login.

entries.title: The train question now shows up wherever a run starts
entries.summary: The choice between your own train designs and the built-in ones is now offered on every route that begins a run — including Minecraft's own Create New World screen, which used to ask only after the world had been built. Backing out with Escape returns you to the menu you came from and creates nothing.
highlights: Create New World from the vanilla menu now asks before the world is generated, like Dungeon Train's own New World button does.
The Train Editor no longer asks. Editor worlds are creative, so they are Free Play anyway and always load your designs.
Dying with immediate respawn on reuses your last answer instead of interrupting the reboard.

entries.title: The vote page lines up with the book again
entries.summary: After reading a community book, the train's vote page sat in the wrong place — its question could land on top of the "Page 2 of 2" line, and at some window sizes the thumbs drifted off the page entirely and stopped responding where you clicked them. The page now follows the book wherever it sits, including when Scribble's centred book layout moves it.
highlights: The train's question no longer collides with the page counter
The thumbs and the report button now click where they are drawn, at every window size and GUI scale

entries.title: Abandoning a run always shows the recap
entries.summary: With the Immediate Respawn game rule on, choosing "Abandon This Run" from the pause menu used to drop you straight into a fresh world, skipping the end-of-run recap entirely. Now it takes you to the death screen like any other run ending, so you can read the recap and choose when to board again. Immediate Respawn also carries over into each new world the train makes for you, instead of quietly switching itself off after the first one.
highlights: Abandon This Run now opens the death screen even with Immediate Respawn on
Dying normally still rolls straight into a fresh world when Immediate Respawn is on
The Immediate Respawn setting now sticks across every world in a run chain

entries.title: Translators can read the whole English string again
entries.summary: The translation editor used to cut the English off after six lines, so the mod's longest strings — the books — could not be read in full by the person being asked to translate them. Nothing is truncated now: the text grows to fit, scrolls when there is more of it, and the divider between it and your translation can be dragged to give either side more room.
highlights: The English on the translate screen is no longer cut off — it scrolls instead
Drag the divider to trade room between the original text and your translation
The "unreviewed machine translation" warning stays visible while you scroll

entries.title: Translation editor explains every variable
entries.summary: In the translation editor, the placeholders in an English string are now underlined, and hovering one says what the game actually puts there with a few real examples. Where the value is itself a translated phrase, the example is shown in the language you are translating into, with the English beside it.
highlights: Placeholders like %s and %1$s are underlined in the English source
Hover a placeholder for what it holds, plus two or three real example values
Examples that are themselves translated show in your language and in English

entries.title: Jump from a translation to its source
entries.summary: The translation editor now shows a View source link beside the English heading. It opens a search of the Dungeon Train repository for that string's key, so you can see where the game actually uses the line you are translating.
highlights: View source link on the heading row of the translation editor
Finds both the English entry and every place the code uses it

entries.title: Library rooms have their books back
entries.summary: Portal library rooms had been turning up with completely bare shelves. They are stocked again — and when nobody has written enough books in your language to fill one, the room now settles for the closest author it can find instead of standing empty. Expect a shorter shelf in that case rather than none at all. A dropped connection to the community book service no longer empties every library in your world for the rest of the session either; a room that comes up short quietly tries again a few minutes later.
highlights: Library rooms are stocked with books again instead of standing bare
If nobody writes enough in your language, the room picks the closest author it can rather than showing nothing — a shorter shelf you can read beats a full one you cannot
A hiccup reaching the community book service no longer leaves every library in the world empty until you restart
A library that finds nobody tries again a few minutes later, so one thin moment no longer settles it

entries.title: Ctrl+Z takes back Effortless Building work in the editor
entries.summary: Building part of a carriage with Effortless Building and then pressing Ctrl+Z used to undo whatever you'd placed by hand before it, leaving the Effortless Building work sitting there. It now goes on the editor's own undo stack like everything else — one press takes back a whole line, cube or mirrored build, and Ctrl+Y puts it back.
highlights: Effortless Building builds and breaks are undoable with the editor's Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y
A whole multi-block build is one press, mirrored copies included
Effortless Building's own undo can itself be taken back
Applies to work inside an editor plot; building out past the plot is unchanged

entries.title: Portal room editor shows where the doors go
entries.summary: Authoring a dimensional carriage room now shows you the two corridor doorways it has to be built around. A translucent door stands in each opening — the same door the corridor really hangs — so a wall across the walkway centre line is something you see while you build rather than something you discover by walking a portal.
highlights: Both corridor doorways are marked in every portal room plot, and follow the room as you resize it.
Toggle them with /dt editor doorghosts on|off — separate from the out-of-plot stray ghosts.

entries.title: The Train Builder (work in progress)
entries.summary: A soft release: the Train Builder is still in development and not yet fully functional, so expect rough edges and unfinished corners. It is a simpler way to build carriages, tracks and tunnels in a dedicated build world, and in time it is meant to replace the more complex Train Editor. For now both are here — hold Shift on the title screen to open the Builder, and find what you have made under My Builds.
highlights: Still in development and not fully functional — this is an early look, not a finished tool.
Intended to replace the more complex Train Editor eventually; until then the Editor remains the complete option.
Hold Shift on the title screen and the Train Editor slot becomes the Train Builder.
A My Builds screen, reachable from the editor menu (X) and the pause menu, lists everything you have saved.
Build in a flat, empty world made for the job, with mirroring, resizable rooms and a live size and weight readout.
Save a whole carriage in one piece — shell and interior together — as well as individual parts, tracks and tunnels.

entries.title: Backpacks keep their contents, and villagers will price your own items
entries.summary: Dungeon Train now ships Edible Backpacks 0.11.0 and requires Trade Everything 0.9.0. The headline fix: anything stored in a backpack slot used to vanish after a relog or a respawn — it now survives both.
highlights: Backpack contents are no longer lost when you relog or respawn.
The Upgraded Backpack recipe now takes a gold block in the middle of the 3x3 of backpacks.
A villager's Trade Anything slot cycles through the items you are carrying, each with its own price.

entries.title: Translate a whole set of variations in one go
entries.summary: A lot of Dungeon Train's text is the same line written many different ways — thirteen wordings of one chat message, thirty-nine narrations for one death, a dozen alternative pages for one book. The translation editor used to list every one of them as an unrelated string. Now it knows they belong together: a button collapses each set into a single row, and inside a string a Next button walks you straight to the next variation that still needs a human, without going back to the list.
highlights: A grouping button beside the search box folds each set of variations into one row, badged with how many there are and how many still need review
Inside a string, a strip says which variation you are on, and Next opens the next one waiting on a translator
Next asks before it moves on if you have unsaved typing — save, discard, or stay
Grouping is off by default; the list you already know is unchanged until you turn it on

entries.title: Hours spent on the engine room ledger
entries.summary: Once running costs and the current goal are both covered, the engine room shows the hours spent building Dungeon Train.

entries.title: PlayerMobs put flint and steel to work
entries.summary: Dungeon Train now requires PlayerMob 0.94.0, and both modpacks ship it: PlayerMobs pick up dropped flint and steel, cook their kills with it, torch enemies mid-fight, and stop to put fires out.

entries.title: Fixed: offhand item duplication
entries.summary: Shift-clicking a stackable item out of your offhand slot no longer duplicates it. The bug doubled the stack every time and affected every player.

entries.title: The Tallyman's books — 29 leaderboards riding the train
entries.summary: A new kind of book turns up in chests: a leaderboard, kept by The Tallyman. Each one covers a single board — furthest carriage, longest aboard, most chests opened, kindest benefactors and twenty-five more — lists the top players on it, and closes by telling you where you stand. If you are not on it, it says so rather than inventing a rank for you. Boards that make sense both ways come in a matched pair, one life and all lives, so you can see whether you are good at a run or good at the game. Among the new ones: distance covered, measured from where you started rather than by how far you have paced up and down a carriage.
highlights: Leaderboard books spawn among the train's other random books
29 boards, many paired as one-life and all-lives
Distance covered now measures how far down the line you got, not steps taken
New boards for people cursed, lovers, most loved, and biggest single gift
Breaking a vase no longer ends a Walk Past The Loot streak — a vase is not loot
Every rank gets two lines, so long names are never truncated to fit a score

entries.title: A heads-up when a connection blocker is in the way
entries.summary: If you run a DPI-bypass tool like zapret or GoodbyeDPI to reach Discord and YouTube, Dungeon Train now tells you once, on the title screen, that it may be sitting between you and brennan.games. Those tools reroute traffic at the driver level, and when they catch DT's traffic the online features don't fail loudly — community books, shared carriages and the rest just quietly never arrive. Now you get told why, instead of wondering where they went.
highlights: One-time notice on the title screen, with a 'Don't show again' if you already know.
The check is local: it looks at the names of running programs on your own PC, and sends nothing anywhere.
Only shown if you've allowed the mod to use the network — otherwise there is nothing to interfere with.

entries.title: Paintings now stay put in dimensional carriages
entries.summary: Paintings and item frames hung in dimensional carriages now stick around properly.
Some of the named pigs riding the train answer to a more famous name. A small tribute, and a rare one — you will not meet one every trip.

entries.title: Dimensional carriage lighting fades instead of jumping
entries.summary: Walking into a dimensional carriage no longer snaps the lighting. The corridor now fades once from the light of the world the train is running through to the light of the room at the far end, so crossing between the carriage and its copy is something you feel rather than something you see happen. Turn it off with the new crossingFade client setting.
highlights: One smooth lighting fade along the corridor instead of a jump
The change is gradual with distance, from the train door to the room door
Turning around mid-corridor no longer flashes the lighting
New crossingFade client setting restores the old hard cut

entries.title: Dimensional carriages can keep their own walls as they repeat
entries.summary: An endless dimensional carriage used to dissolve its own walls as it repeated — the wall between two copies was carved away so the space read as one continuous hall, taking whatever the builder had put on it with it. Rooms can now be built the other way instead: every copy keeps the walls it was drawn with, and you walk between copies through the doorways the builder left. Existing rooms are untouched.
highlights: New Room Walls setting on a dimensional carriage: Merged (as before) or Kept
Kept rooms repeat their walls exactly, including the wall the way back to the train stands in
The library dimension now keeps its walls

entries.title: The Tallyman's books turn up all over the train
entries.summary: Leaderboard books are no longer something you mostly find on a bookshelf. They now surface across the train's chests, pots and villager stashes, so a board can turn up wherever you are rather than only where the books are kept. Where a container already offered reading matter, the leaderboard book takes a share of that rather than adding to it, so your odds of finding some book are unchanged — only which book shifts.
highlights: Leaderboard books can now be found in fishing, mining, villager, ore and pottery loot
Villager stashes get their first book of any kind
A leaderboard book can appear in the starting chest

entries.title: The Free Play badge says why it's on
entries.summary: Hover the Free Play effect in your inventory and it now tells you what turned it on — the game mode you switched to, the command you ran, a changed setting, a cheat mod it found. Before, that reason was said once in chat and then scrolled away, so joining a world that was already in Free Play left you with a badge and no explanation. The tooltip also got shorter: the reason leads, the consequences fit on one line.
highlights: The Free Play tooltip names what triggered it, including settings changed or cheat mods detected
The reason survives logging out, so a world you come back to still explains itself

entries.title: Container menu now shows item icons
entries.summary: The container contents menu (C) lists each item by its inventory icon instead of its name, so rows stay compact and long item names no longer spill across the count and weight columns. Click an icon to reveal that item's name beside it; click again to hide it.
highlights: Item rows lead with the inventory icon — narrower panel, no overlapping text
Click an icon to reveal its name; only that row's column widens

entries.title: Faulthurst leaves you a note about your own run
entries.summary: A new book turns up in the train's loot, signed by Faulthurst. It greets you by name and names one real number from your current life — the carriage you've reached, how long you've been aboard, how many chests you've opened, the longest stretch you went without opening a thing. The number stays live while you carry the book and freezes the moment you read it, so what you find inside is your run exactly as it stood when you opened it.
highlights: Eighteen things he might remark on, twelve of them the one-life half of a leaderboard board.
He never mentions something that hasn't happened — a number has to be worth a page before he'll write it down.
Seven ways he opens and twenty ways he signs off, from "Keep it up." to "Why?"
Written in every language Dungeon Train speaks.

entries.title: A book that counts, and a room full of them
entries.summary: Chests, pots and bookshelves now turn up Stats Books. Open one and it is a coin-flip: either a tall leaderboard, ranking every player on the train and closing on where you stand — or a short note from Faulthurst about your own run, naming one real number from it. You never know which until you read it. Dimensional carriages can now be stocked with the whole tally instead of one author's writing: every leaderboard and every run stat the train keeps, 47 books, shelved in one room with a note on the lectern explaining what you have walked into. Room authors set how often that happens in the Books screen.
highlights: New Stats Book, found in loot — half leaderboard, half a note about your own run
Leaderboard books moved out of the random-book pool onto their own loot entry
Dimensional carriages can shelve the complete tally: 29 leaderboards + 18 run stats
Stats joins Self, Player and Signature as a fourth share in a room's Books mix

entries.title: Test the dimensional carriage you're building
entries.summary: Room authors get a Test the Carriage button in the editor menu. It stamps the dimensional carriage you have open — room, a corridor either side, its own walls mode, block variants, lighting and fog — and puts you in the doorway looking down it. The room repeats around you as you walk, the way it does on the train. Back returns you to the plot and clears it away.
highlights: Shows in the editor menu while a dimensional carriage is open
No train needed — nothing to ride to and nothing to wait for
Same tiling, block variants, lighting and fog as the real thing

entries.title: Leaving the dimensional carriage editor works again
entries.summary: Exiting the editor after opening a dimensional carriage directly now returns you to where you came from, in the game mode you were in. Before, it told you there was no session to exit and left you standing in the plot in creative.
highlights: Only affected going straight to a room — /dungeontrain editor portals, or a room plot's Enter Inside
