entries.title: Discord announcements link to the release they announce
entries.summary: The release announcement in Discord now opens that exact build's release page. It used to open the Downloads page, which always showed the newest build — so an older announcement sent you somewhere else.

entries.title: See who wrote a book as it burns
entries.summary: Dungeon Train books burn away after you read them, and until now their author burned with them. Turn on Book Author Chat and every book that catches fire — one you just read, one you threw away unread, one dropped on death — names its writer in chat: "The book by X burns". Off by default; the toggle is in Options > Dungeon Train and in the X menu > Options.
highlights: New Book Author Chat option, off by default
Credits the author of every Dungeon Train book as it burns
Per-player: your setting, your chat, on servers too

entries.title: Nineteen languages catch up with the game
entries.summary: Whole features had been reaching non-English players in English: the book-vote replies, the carriage builder, the Free Play and settings-changed notices, the video tools, custom content, and the translation editor's own controls. Every one of the nineteen translated languages now has the full set of the game's text — around 4,460 lines that were simply missing.
highlights: All 19 languages are now complete against English — no missing lines left in any of them
Newly filled lines are marked as machine translation in the in-game translation editor, so speakers can find and fix them
Simplified Chinese also gains the two Adventure Item Names buttons it was short

entries.title: Keeping your inventory on death is Free Play
entries.summary: A world that has run with Keep Inventory on is now Free Play — permanently, even if you turn the rule back off.

entries.title: The book-author chat line speaks every language too
entries.summary: The v0.673.0 book-author setting and the Stats Book shipped English-only. Both are now translated into all nineteen languages, along with the chat line that names whoever wrote a book as it burns.
highlights: Book Author Chat, its description, the Stats Book name and the burn line are translated in all 19 languages

entries.title: Close the editor's Welcome panel
entries.summary: The Train Editor's Welcome board now has a close (X) button, top-right. Your choice is remembered per player, per world.
highlights: X button closes the Welcome board
Editor menu's Welcome Panel toggle brings it back

entries.title: Your builds now upload and can go on the train
entries.summary: Saving a build in the Train Builder or Train Editor now uploads it to your builder profile, so it follows you between worlds and a finished carriage can be submitted to the train for everyone. Before, "My Builds" told every player that builder profiles were off on their world — the switch shipped off, no server ever turned it on, and so nobody's build was ever uploaded anywhere.
highlights: Uploading still needs Internet Connection on (Options → Dungeon Train), and a build stays private to you until you choose to submit it
If you deliberately turned builder profiles off, they stay off
"My Builds" now says when it's your own Internet Connection setting rather than the world's, instead of blaming the world for both

entries.title: Spectator cinematic no longer leaves you frozen
entries.summary: Replaying the intro cinematic from spectator mode could leave you unable to move, with /kill and reboarding the only way out. Fixed. The hotkey can also be switched off now in Options → Dungeon Train…, and it finally shows a readable name in Controls.

entries.title: Copy an author's name from the burn line
entries.summary: In the Book Author Chat line, click the author's name to copy it.

entries.title: One Death Note per target per life
entries.summary: A second Death Note naming a player you've already noted this life no longer arms a second echo. The repeat book still burns, now telling you they've already been death noted this life. Love Notes follow the same rule, tracked separately from Death Notes.
highlights: One echo per named target per life, not one per note signed
A repeat note still burns, with a clear message instead of a silent extra echo
Death Notes and Love Notes are tracked separately, so one of each on the same person still works

entries.title: Editor menus get an Auto mode and a render-distance dial
entries.summary: The editor's world-space menus now default to Auto, hiding other plots' panels while you work in one. A new Menu Distance setting on the X-menu caps how far any editor menu draws.
highlights: Auto is the new default for Editor Menus
New Menu Distance setting on the X-menu (default 128)

entries.title: No weather in the End band
entries.summary: Rain and lightning no longer follow you into the End band — the void stretch is silent and clear, whatever the weather is doing back in the overworld.

entries.title: Cheats being available is Free Play
entries.summary: A world where cheats are available to anyone playing is now Free Play for as long as that is true — advancements still earn live, but they don't add to your profile and global stats don't accrue. If you had cheats yourself, your run stays Free Play afterwards.

entries.title: Shift-click twice in the creative menu to fill your hotbar
entries.summary: Shift-clicking an item in the creative menu still hands you a full stack on the cursor. Shift-click the same item again and that stack drops straight into your hotbar - and keep clicking to fill the slots along from there.
highlights: The second shift-click on an item puts the stack in your hotbar: your selected slot if it is free, otherwise the first empty one.
Every further click on that same item fills the next slot along, wrapping around to the start.
Clicking a different item starts over, and the first shift-click behaves exactly as it always has.

entries.title: No more ice pillars in the End band
entries.summary: Stray towers of packed ice no longer generate beside the track when the train crosses the End band. The band's void chunks skipped their terrain fill but still ran the surface pass, so a frozen ocean underneath could stamp iceberg pillars into the void — and the strip of world that protects the track from the erosion kept them standing right where you ride past.
highlights: The End band is clean void, islands and chorus again — no ice

entries.title: Finish and sign books left on ordinary lecterns
entries.summary: A book & quill you leave on a plain lectern is now a draft you can come back to: right-click the lectern empty-handed to pick it up and keep writing, then sign it to seal it as a letter. Pressing Done leaves the book on the lectern exactly as you wrote it — your text is kept, nothing is handed back to you, and the book is no longer renamed behind your back.
highlights: Right-click a lectern empty-handed to pick a draft back up and finish it
Done keeps the text you just typed instead of discarding it
Drafts rest on the lectern unchanged — no surprise rename, and no duplicate book in creative

entries.title: The editor menu is now a proper screen, with tabs
entries.summary: Pressing X in the editor opens a real menu with a mouse cursor instead of a panel floating in the world that you aimed your head at. Its rows are grouped into four tabs — File, Current, Settings and Nav — so you are not scanning thirty rows to find one. Your hotbar stays live underneath, so you can still pick the block a row is about to use.
highlights: Point and click with a cursor — no more aiming your head at a floating panel
Rows grouped into File, Current, Settings and Nav; tabs with nothing in them are hidden
The hotbar keeps working while the menu is open — scroll it or press 1-9
Long lists scroll instead of running off the bottom of the screen

entries.title: Empty carriages no longer turn up in the train
entries.summary: A leftover test template was shipping with the mod, and it could be picked for any carriage slot like a normal one. When it was, you got a completely empty carriage — no floor, no walls, no roof, nothing inside — a gap in the middle of the train you could fall straight through. It has been removed, so every carriage the train builds is a real one.
highlights: Removed the empty test carriage from the pool of carriages the train can build
It no longer appears as a blank template in the carriage editor

entries.title: Builds are submitted for review
entries.summary: Your saved builds go to your builder profile on the server, and a finished carriage can be submitted for review. Community carriages are paused on the train in the meantime.

entries.title: Dungeon Train options screen redone with tabs
entries.summary: The Dungeon Train settings screen (Options → Dungeon Train…) no longer runs off the bottom of the window. Settings are now split across three tabs — General, Train and Editor — each scrolling on its own with Done always reachable.
highlights: Three tabs instead of one long column: General, Train, Editor
The list scrolls and Done stays reachable at any window size or GUI scale
Internet Connection row temporarily removed (could not be turned back on)

entries.title: Choose how each editor menu appears
entries.summary: The Train Editor's four menus can each be shown either as a panel floating in the world that you aim at, or as a window on your screen that you point at with the mouse. Pick per menu under Options > Dungeon Train > Editor, or from the X menu's own Options. The X and V menus act on the whole build, so they open on screen where the cursor is more precise. The C and Z menus edit a single block, so they stay out in the world beside the block you're editing.
highlights: The X menu can be a floating in-world panel again — it became a screen window last update, and now that's a choice rather than the only option.
The V, C and Z menus can all be screen windows with a free mouse cursor.
Your hotbar keeps working while a screen menu is open, so the V menu's Swap still takes whatever block you're holding.
Each menu remembers its own setting, and a change takes effect the next time you open that menu.

entries.title: Shulker Box Tooltip added to the modpack
entries.summary: The modpack now ships Shulker Box Tooltip. Hover any shulker box — or other container item — to see what's inside without placing it down, which saves a lot of digging through loot on the train.
highlights: Hover a shulker box to preview its contents
Enabled by default; can be switched off in the launcher

entries.title: Clumps bundled in the modpack
entries.summary: Both modpacks now ship Clumps, which merges nearby XP orbs into one so big fights drop a single combined orb instead of a laggy spray. It is on by default but optional — you can disable it in your launcher if you prefer vanilla orbs.
highlights: XP orbs merge together, reducing lag from big mob fights
Enabled by default in the CurseForge and Modrinth packs; safe to turn off

entries.title: Better Advancements support, and it ships with the modpack
entries.summary: The modpack now bundles Better Advancements, which replaces the advancements screen with a zoomable, searchable one. Dungeon Train's advancement tree works properly inside it: advancements you have unlocked the path to show their real icon, unearned ones still keep their secrets — you get the hint, not the description, and not the criteria behind it either. Scrolling a tall tree now reaches the whole thing, with a little room past each end. If you play without Better Advancements nothing changes.
highlights: Better Advancements bundled with the modpack, enabled by default
The Dungeon Train advancement tree renders correctly in its screen
Unearned advancements keep showing hints instead of spoilers
Scrolling reaches the bottom of a tall advancement tree

entries.title: Clearing a dimensional carriage in the editor really clears it
entries.summary: The editor's Clear on a dimensional carriage left the room standing: it wiped the plot and then stamped the built-in room straight back over it, and the block variants it said it had removed reappeared the next time the plot was stamped. Clear now leaves the plot empty inside its cage, keeps the room's authored size, and the variants it drops stay dropped.
highlights: Clear empties the plot instead of replacing your build with the built-in room.
Cleared block variants no longer come back on the next stamp.
A cleared room now shows as unsaved, so saving makes the clear permanent.

entries.title: Stats books burn after reading, like every other book
entries.summary: Leaderboard boards and Faulthurst's notes were the only books on the train you could keep. They now catch fire once you've read them, the same as a random chest book — and a board found in a chest could never burn at all until now.
highlights: Leaderboard books and Faulthurst stat notes burn after reading
Fixed: a leaderboard book rolled from a chest was the one book in the game that could never burn
A book nobody has picked up still won't ignite — a broken chest, or a Stat Room's shelves, stay safe

entries.title: Portal room editor plots are lit by the room's own sky
entries.summary: Building a dimensional carriage no longer means building it in the dark. A room's Sky setting — Daylight, Day/Night, Nether or End — now lights its editor plot the same way it will light the room once it is riding the train, so what you author is what you get without walking a test session first. A new Plot Lighting switch in the editor's X-menu Settings tab turns it off for anyone who wants the unlit box back while they place their own light sources. Skybox blocks stopped casting a shadow, too: a hole punched through to the sky now lets light through it, which is what it looked like it should have been doing all along.
highlights: A portal room's Sky setting now lights its editor plot
Plot Lighting switch in the X-menu Settings tab (on by default)
Skybox blocks let light through instead of shadowing the floor below

entries.title: One more advancement
entries.summary: There is one more advancement in the game.

entries.title: Your builds and progress now survive a modpack update
entries.summary: Updating the modpack could delete every carriage you'd built in the Train Editor and every advancement you'd earned. Dungeon Train kept them in the config folder, and modpack launchers replace that folder when a pack updates. They now live alongside your worlds, where an update can't touch them, and your existing files are moved across automatically the first time you launch.
highlights: Train Editor builds, advancements, stats and loadouts moved out of the config folder to a place modpack updates leave alone.
Dungeon Train now keeps rolling backups of your builds and progress — when you load a world, when you save a build in the Train Editor, when you die, and when you leave.
Already lost your builds to an update? At the title screen Dungeon Train will offer to restore them from a backup or from an older install on your PC. /dtbackup and /dtrestore do the same in-game.

entries.title: Dungeon Train speaks Romanian
entries.summary: Romanian joins the language list — the whole game, not just the menus: every screen, the item names, and all 57 in-game books. It is machine translation nobody has proofread yet, and the language list says so with the faded AI mark; if you read Romanian, the in-game translation editor is open and your fixes come back to everyone.
highlights: Romanian (Română) is selectable in the vanilla language list
Menus, HUD, advancements, item names and all 57 books translated
Counts follow real Romanian grammar — 1 vagon, 3 vagoane, 20 de vagoane
Marked AI-unreviewed, so every line is open for community correction

entries.title: Choose where your backups are kept
entries.summary: Dungeon Train's backups of your builds and progress used to live inside your Minecraft instance. That is likely safe from a modpack update, but not always — and it is no protection at all if the instance itself is deleted or reset. There's now a Backups setting in Options > Dungeon Train: On keeps a copy outside the instance so nothing an update or a reinstall does can reach it, Instanced keeps them inside it, and Off turns them off.
highlights: New Backups option in Options > Dungeon Train — On / Instanced / Off, with each choice explained when you hover it.
On (the default) keeps a copy outside your Minecraft folder, so reinstalling or resetting the instance no longer loses your builds.
Server owners can set backups without the in-game menu: launch with -Ddungeontrain.backups=off (or DUNGEONTRAIN_BACKUPS=off), which accepts on / instanced / off.

entries.title: The game now counts the time you spend building
entries.summary: Hours in the Train Builder used to count for nothing — every stat Dungeon Train kept was about riding. Time spent building is now tracked and ranked, alongside a board for the builds you have had approved onto other people's trains.
highlights: Time in a Train Builder world, and time up at the editor plots, both count towards your building time.
Two new leaderboard books: Longest Building, and Most Builds Approved.
A Stat Room now stocks more books to match.

entries.title: TrashSlot joins the modpack
entries.summary: The modpack now ships TrashSlot, an optional inventory trash slot for binning junk without hunting for lava. It arrives switched off — tick it on in the launcher's optional-mods list whenever you want it.
highlights: Drag-and-drop trash slot on most inventory screens
Off by default — opt in from the launcher, no reinstall needed

entries.title: OH MY LORD I DID IT! I FIXED THE BACKWARD BUG
entries.summary: This dam bug has been plaguing me for months. Since the start of this project, I wanted the train to go infinitely backwards. Well today, I am proud to say - it goes a god dam long way backwards! How far? Im sure one of you will tell me if its not infinite. Please go forth and explore! Sincerely, Brennan.

entries.title: Load your builds from your profile into the editor
entries.summary: My Builds could always show you what you had made — including builds from another world, another save, or another machine — but it could never open one. Now it can. Load into Editor pulls the build down, puts it in your template library and takes you straight to it, switching the editor to the right category on the way. If you already have a build by that name, it asks what you want: replace the one you have, rename the one you have, or load this one under a new name.
highlights: Load into Editor on the My Builds screen
Works for builds this world has never seen — a new save, a reinstall, a new machine
Every kind: carriages, groups, rooms, parts, track and portal rooms
Takes you to the build when it lands, changing editor category if it has to
A name you already use asks what to do instead of refusing

entries.title: Night and sunrise skybox blocks
entries.summary: Two more skies to punch a window through to. The Night Skybox Block is night on both halves of the day: the stars wheel overhead and the moon crosses with the right phase, but the sun never comes up, so a room built around one stays under a night sky no matter what time it is outside. The Sunrise Skybox Block holds a permanent dawn and turns sideways the way the upside-down skybox does, with the sun and its glow sweeping right around the horizon instead of climbing, the moon trailing opposite and the stars turning with them.
highlights: New Night Skybox Block: stars, moon and phase, and no sunrise ever
New Sunrise Skybox Block: a dawn that orbits the horizon sideways
Both work anywhere the other skybox blocks do, carriage walls included

entries.title: Control how many backups you keep, and clear them
entries.summary: Dungeon Train keeps backups of your builds and progress, and until now it decided on its own how many to hold on to. It now keeps a set number per version — five by default — so you can tell at a glance what you have, and there is a button to delete them all and reclaim the space.
highlights: A Backups section in Options > Dungeon Train, with a slider for how many backups to keep per version.
Clear Backups shows how much disk your backups are using and deletes them, inside and outside your Minecraft folder, after confirming.

entries.title: TrashSlot now comes installed, and stays out of the way
entries.summary: TrashSlot is now part of the pack proper rather than an optional extra you had to tick on. It ships quiet: there is no trash slot in your inventory and none of its keys are bound, so nothing about your screens or your controls changes unless you want it to. To use it, bind a key to Show/Hide TrashSlot under Options then Controls, and press it with a screen open.
highlights: Installed with the pack — no optional-mods tick needed
Ships with the slot hidden and every TrashSlot key unbound, so your inventory and controls look exactly as they did
Bind Show/Hide TrashSlot in Options then Controls to turn it on

entries.title: Turn your own train builds on or off from the main menu
entries.summary: If you have builds of your own from the Train Editor, the main menu now carries a switch for them, sitting just left of New Game. Lit means your designs ride the train — and those runs stay Free Play, so stats and advancements keep to that world. Grey means the built-in designs ride instead, and everything you do counts. Flipping it also settles the question for good: worlds stop stopping to ask which train you want. Options → Custom Train Content puts the question back if you'd rather be asked each time. The prompt itself now leads with the choice that keeps your stats.
highlights: Main-menu switch for your own train builds, shown only when you have some
Pressing it retires the per-world 'which train?' prompt
That prompt now offers Default Train (Live) first

entries.title: The carriage at the edge of view stops changing on you
entries.summary: A single carriage near the edge of your render distance could quietly rebuild itself as a different type, from a different stage, when it reloaded. It now comes back as the carriage that was there. Carriages that slip out of line are also pulled back into place instead of being abandoned mid-train.
highlights: A reloading carriage keeps the stage and the build it was made with, instead of re-rolling against wherever the train has since travelled.
A carriage that ends up badly out of line is put back in one move, rather than inching toward the train and giving up.
Carriages either side of one that is still settling keep moving with the train, so the two cannot drift apart while it beds in.

entries.title: Editor: category switching skips the save prompt
entries.summary: The "Save before switch?" list flagged templates nobody had edited, so it is bypassed for now. Save with /dt save before switching — the switch re-stamps every plot.

entries.title: Community carriages now ride your train
entries.summary: Carriages other players built and changed while riding now turn up in your run. A shared slot leases an approved build from the pool, places it, and hands it back with whatever you changed in it — so a room you rearrange travels on to somebody else's train, credited to everyone who has worked on it. Train Builder builds stay separate for now: they still upload to My Builds and can be submitted, but they aren't placed into runs yet.
highlights: Community-built carriages appear in runs (shared slots lease from the pool)
Your edits to a leased carriage travel back to the pool, credited by name
Train Builder submissions are held back — a separate system, opening later

entries.title: Turn the backpack button on or off
entries.summary: The backpack panels' open/close button on your inventory screen can now be switched off from Dungeon Train's own options, and it is a little smaller than before. Hiding it costs you nothing: the panels still open with the Edible Backpacks key, which you can bind under Controls.
highlights: A new Backpack Button setting under Options -> Dungeon Train... -> General shows or hides the button.
The button itself is smaller, so it sits over the inventory without reading as another piece of GUI furniture.
Shift-clicking an item now fills your hotbar and inventory first, and only overflows into the backpack panels.
The Upgraded Backpack advancement now describes the real recipe: eight backpacks around a gold block.

entries.title: Approved player translations flow back into the game automatically
entries.summary: Translations players submit in-game and that get approved are served by the relay straight away, but until now they never made it into the mod itself — so they vanished on an offline launch and their authors went uncredited in the jar. A weekly job now pulls approved work back into the build for review.
highlights: Approved player translations are collected weekly instead of by hand
Translators must be registered with their credit before their work can be merged

entries.title: Internal improvements
entries.summary: Behind-the-scenes maintenance work. Nothing to see or do differently in game.

entries.title: Two runaway relay requests that were costing you frame time
entries.summary: Standing in a Stat Room, or riding past a community carriage, was quietly making the game ask the server the same thing over and over — twenty times a second, for the rest of the session. Two separate faults, both fixed. A Stat Room waiting on a leaderboard the server has no scores for yet now waits politely instead of asking on every tick, and a community carriage you have never touched no longer uploads a copy of itself moments after it appears. If reactions felt sluggish lately — chests opening slowly, hits not landing, items not picking up — this is a large part of why.
highlights: Fixed: a leaderboard with no scores yet was re-requested every tick, forever
Fixed: every community carriage uploaded itself on arrival, even untouched
Stat Rooms still fill in as their boards arrive, just without the churn
Your own edits to a community carriage still sync exactly as before

entries.title: The leaderboards are for real runs again
entries.summary: Someone in Free Play could fly to the edge of the world and take the top of a leaderboard with it. "Furthest Distance, One Life" was led by a 29,999,728m walk that nobody walked. Free Play runs no longer score on any board — the game already knew a run had gone into creative, it just wasn't telling the leaderboards. Your own stats and death records are unaffected, and Free Play still works exactly as it did; it simply stops competing with people playing it straight. The one-life boards were the ones affected: distance, time aboard, carriages reached, chests opened, pacifist run, friends made, echoes put down, and walking past the loot. The all-lives boards were already safe.
highlights: Free Play runs are no longer ranked on any leaderboard
The bogus world-border distance records are being removed
Nothing changes about how Free Play itself plays

entries.title: Armor trim templates are finally worth trading
entries.summary: Pulling a Silence or Wayfinder template out of a carriage felt like a find, and then the villager offered you a single item for it — the same as a stick. Minecraft marks every armor trim template as ordinary, so Trade Everything had been pricing them at the bare minimum. They are now worth 2.2 emeralds apiece in the Trade Anything slot, which works out to 26 items in trade. All eighteen templates, including Flow and Bolt.
highlights: Every armor trim smithing template now values at 2.2 emeralds, up from 1/16th
Covers all eighteen, and any a datapack adds
The Netherite upgrade template is untouched — it is not an armor trim
Only applies when Trade Everything is installed; it ships with the modpack

entries.title: Leaderboards now start from scores the game can vouch for
entries.summary: The last update stopped Free Play runs from being ranked, but it could only do that for runs recorded after it shipped — every score already on a board predated the check, including a 29,999,728m walk that was really a flight to the edge of the world. Rather than delete anyone's history, those scores are now kept but unranked, and the boards rebuild from runs the game can actually vouch for. Expect the one-life boards to look sparse at first and fill in over the following days as players update and finish a run. Most Books Written and Most Advancements are unaffected, because those are counted by the server rather than reported by the game. Nothing has been erased — your stats, death records and Stat Room shelves are all exactly as they were.
highlights: Old scores are retained but no longer ranked, including the bogus ones
Boards refill from verified runs over the days after this update
Most Books Written and Most Advancements are unchanged
Playing on an older version means your runs won't be ranked until you update

entries.title: Abandoning a run now asks first
entries.summary: The pause menu's red "Abandon This Run" button used to kill you on the first click. It now asks, and says outright what abandoning means: your character dies, it counts as a death, and there is no undo.
highlights: A confirmation step between the button and the kill — no more losing a long run to a stray click.
Escape or "Go back" leaves the run exactly as it was; only the red confirm ends it.

entries.title: A couple of new advancements
entries.summary: A couple of new hidden advancements have been added.

entries.title: No more falling mobs at the edges of the upside-down zone
entries.summary: Ambient mobs could still spawn in the fade zones right before and after the upside-down stretch of track, where the mirrored terrain is only partially formed — they'd spawn with nothing solid underfoot and fall to their death. Those edges are now covered by the same no-spawn rule as the upside-down band itself.

entries.title: New supporter names in the item name pool
entries.summary: Adventure Item Names 0.52.0 brings a new Discord supporter into the name pool in five forms — sstasske, Staske, Stas, Stanislav, Stanislav The Russian — plus Testificate, the name Notch left on villagers in the Beta 1.9 pre-releases, and a spelling fix for supporter TJYongHeng.

entries.title: The upside-down world is upside-down again — with shaders on
entries.summary: If you play with Sodium or Iris shaders — which the modpack ships — the upside-down stretch was quietly rendering the right way up. The world now hangs from the ceiling as it should, whether or not a shaderpack is loaded, while the train stays upright underneath you.
highlights: Fixed: upside-down band terrain rendered upright for anyone running Sodium or Iris shaders
The flip now looks identical with shaders on and off
Terrain right beside the track flips too, not just the far hills

entries.title: Fixed mobs getting stuck behind in endless dimensional carriage rooms
entries.summary: Mobs that wandered into a room copy that later retired could get left behind instead of being cleaned up. Fixed.

entries.title: Advancement tweaks
entries.summary: A few advancement adjustments.

entries.title: End cities are rarer
entries.summary: End cities in the End band now generate about 5× less often.

entries.title: Difficulty potion effects now show as infinite
entries.summary: Buffed mobs on the train carry their difficulty potion effects permanently, but the effect readout showed a nonsensical multi-thousand-hour countdown instead of the infinity symbol. The effects were always meant to be permanent — now they are marked as such, so Jade and the vanilla effect display both read the infinity symbol.
highlights: Difficulty potion effects on train mobs read as infinite instead of an absurd hour count

entries.title: Enchantment tooltips now explain what each enchantment does
entries.summary: The modpack now ships Enchantment Descriptions, switched on by default. Hover any enchanted item and each enchantment carries a short plain-English line explaining what it actually does — handy when a train chest hands you something you've never rolled before. Its two library dependencies, Bookshelf and Prickle, ship enabled alongside it.
highlights: Enchantment Descriptions bundled and enabled by default
Enchanted item tooltips now explain each enchantment's effect

entries.title: Durability numbers on item tooltips
entries.summary: The modpack now ships Durability Tooltip, switched on by default: hover any tool, weapon or piece of armour and its remaining durability is written out as a number — 'Durability: 137 / 250' — coloured green through orange to red as it wears down, instead of squinting at the damage bar. Its required library, SuperMartijn642's Config Lib, ships alongside it. You can change the style to a bar or plain words, or turn it off, in the mod's config.
highlights: Durability Tooltip bundled and enabled by default
Remaining durability shown as coloured numbers on tool, weapon and armour tooltips

entries.title: Portal corridors fade instead of switching at the door
entries.summary: Walking a portal carriage now changes over the whole walk rather than in the single step through the far door. The fog, the corridor's own light and a daylit room's brightness all shift together as you go, easing in as you leave the train and settling a block before you reach the room — so arriving is a non-event instead of a visible switch.
highlights: Fog and lighting now shift across the whole corridor, not at the doorway
Eased at both ends, so leaving the train and reaching the room are both gentle
The step through the portal room's door no longer changes what you see

entries.title: Dimensional carriage doorways can be moved off centre
entries.summary: The two doorways into a dimensional carriage used to be pinned to the exact middle of the room's end walls, at floor level, on every room ever built. Builders can now put them where they want: hold a door and right-click the doorway marker, and both doorways move to where you aimed — along the wall and up it. Nothing is placed; the door in your hand is just a pointer, which is what lets a doorway sit anywhere rather than only where a door would have something to stand on. How far it can move depends on how much bigger the room is than the corridor running into it, since the corridor still has to be sealed inside the room's walls — a room built at the smallest legal size has nowhere to move it to, and the game now tells you that, and what to grow to get the room.
highlights: Hold a door and right-click a doorway marker to set where the doorways sit
Doorways move both across the end wall and up it
Wider and taller rooms give the doorways more room to move
Rooms built before this are untouched — their doorways stay exactly where they were

entries.title: Traps are remembered
entries.summary: Setting a trap in a drifting carriage, for whoever comes through next, leaves a mark on the temperament your echo is born with.

entries.title: Shulker boxes can't be placed in dimensional carriages
entries.summary: A dimensional carriage exists twice — the corridor you walk through and a hidden copy of it — and the two are kept identical block for block so the crossing between them stays invisible. A shulker box placed in one was copied into the other as an empty box, which could duplicate the item and lose what you had stored in it. Shulker boxes are now refused in both copies, with a word from the box itself in chat. Portal rooms are unaffected.
highlights: Shulker boxes are refused inside a dimensional carriage and its copy
Closes a duplication bug caused by the carriage's hidden copy
Portal rooms are unaffected — shulker boxes work there as normal
